children.translated_text: Now we shall state the procedure.
That, moreover, is known through the transmitted sacred tradition.

children.text: āmnāyaḥ punar mantrāś ca brāhmaṇāni ca ||
children.translated_text: The transmitted tradition, again, consists of mantras and brāhmaṇa texts.

children.text: tad yathābrāhmaṇaṃ vidhir evaṃ karmaliṅgā mantrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, where the brāhmaṇa gives the rule, the mantras whose marks indicate the act are to be used accordingly.
Likewise when it has another purpose.
Likewise, mantras whose indications are those of a brāhmaṇa passage are to be used.
In the absence of that, established tradition is authority.
Because the brāhmaṇa texts have been handed down as authoritative.
We shall explain the <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice).
It is for the gods and for the ancestors.
Facing east, he performs it silently.
For the gods he wears the sacred thread in the <s>yajñopavīta</s> position.
For the ancestors he wears it in the <s>prācīnavīta</s> position.
For the gods, the direction is east or north.
For the ancestors, it is south.
For the gods, the completion is toward the northeast.
For the ancestors, the completion is toward the southwest.
For the ancestors the act is performed once.
For the gods the lower limit is three times.
Or else as prescribed.
The customary movement for the gods is to the right.
For the ancestors it is to the left.
The gods receive offerings accompanied by <s>svāhā</s> and <s>vaṣaṭ</s>.
The ancestors receive offerings accompanied by <s>svadhā</s> and reverential salutation.
For the ancestors the sacrificial grass is cut near the root.
For the gods it is cut at the joints.

children.text: pra yaccha parśum iti darbhāhārāya dātraṃ prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: Saying, 'Hand over the axe,' he hands over the sickle for bringing the darbha grass.

children.text: oṣadhīr dāntu parvan ityupari parvaṇāṃ lūtvā tūṣṇīm āhṛtyottarato 'gner upasādayati ||
children.translated_text: Saying, 'Let the plants cut at the joint,' he cuts above the joints, brings it silently, and places it north of the fire.
He should not turn around the fire in the contrary direction.
He should not pass between the implements of the sacrifice.
Bending the right knee, he offers oblations.

children.text: yā pūrvā paurṇamāsī sānumatir yottarā sā rākā ||
children.translated_text: The earlier full-moon day is <s>Anumati</s>; the later one is <s>Rākā</s>.

children.text: yā pūrvāmāvāsyā sā sinīvālī yottarā sā kuhūḥ ||
children.translated_text: The earlier new-moon day is <s>Sinīvālī</s>; the later one is <s>Kuhū</s>.
Saying, 'Today is the fast-day,' one who is about to observe the fast eats the fasting meal.
It excludes honey, salt, meat, and beans.

children.text: mamāgne varcaḥ iti samidha ādhāya vratam upaiti ||
children.translated_text: Having placed the fuel-stick on the fire with the formula, '<s>Agni</s>, my radiance,' he undertakes the vow.
Or with, 'With the vow, O lord of vows, I approach you.'
He is a celibate student and one under a vow.
He should sleep on the ground.

children.text: prātarhute 'gnau karmaṇe vāṃ veṣāya vāṃ sukṛtāya vām iti pāṇī prakṣālyāpareṇāgner darbhān āstīrya teṣūttaram ānaḍuhaṃ rohitaṃ carma prāggrīvam uttaraloma prastīrya pavitre kurute ||
children.translated_text: When the morning oblation has been made in the fire, saying, 'For your work, for your garment, for your good deed,' he washes his hands, spreads darbha grass west of the fire, and upon it spreads, with the neck toward the east and the hair upward, a red hide of a castrated bull; then he makes the two strainers.

children.text: darbhāvaprachinnāntau prakṣālyānulomam anumārṣṭi viṣṇor manasā pūte sthaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Having washed two darbha blades whose ends are not cut off, he wipes them with the grain, saying, 'By the mind of <s>Viṣṇu</s> you are purified.'

children.text: tvaṃ bhūmim aty eṣy ojasā tvaṃ vedyāṃ sīdasi cārur adhvare tvāṃ pavitram ṛṣayo bharantas tvaṃ punīhi duritāny asmat iti pavitre antardhāya havir nirvapati devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: Placing the two strainers within, saying, 'With strength you pass over the earth; you sit beautifully on the altar in the rite; you, the strainer which the seers bear, purify away our evils,' he measures out the oblation with, 'At the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I measure you out, acceptable.'
In the same way, with the words, 'For <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>.'
On the new-moon day, with the words, 'For <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.'
The offering to <s>Agni</s> always comes first.

children.text: niruptaṃ pavitrābhyāṃ prokṣati amuṣmai tvā juṣṭam yathādevatam ||
children.translated_text: When it has been measured out, he sprinkles it with the two strainers, saying, 'For so-and-so, I sprinkle you as acceptable,' according to the deity.

children.text: ulūkhalamusalaṃ śūrpaṃ prakṣālitaṃ carmaṇyādhāya vrīhīn ulūkhala opyāvaghnaṃs trir haviṣkṛtā vācaṃ visṛjati haviṣkṛd ā dravehi iti ||
children.translated_text: Having washed the mortar, pestle, and winnowing basket and placed them on the hide, he pours the rice into the mortar; while pounding, he releases speech three times, saying, 'O maker of the oblation, run hither.'

children.text: avahatya suphalīkṛtān kṛtvā triḥ prakṣālya taṇḍulān agne varur yajñiyas tvādhi arukṣat iti carum adhidadhāti ||
children.translated_text: After pounding, making the grains well winnowed, and washing the rice three times, he puts on the <s>caru</s> (rice offering), saying, '<s>Agni</s>, worthy of sacrifice, has mounted upon you as the chooser.'
He pours in water with, 'Purified, cleansed.'
For the rice grains, he says, 'Purified by <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: pari tvāgne puraṃ vayam iti triḥ paryagni karoti ||
children.translated_text: With, 'Around you, O <s>Agni</s>, we make a fortress,' he carries fire around it three times.
With the stirring-stick he stirs it upward three times to the right.
After that, it is as desired.
He places the fuel north of the fire.
The sacrificial grass is placed to the north.
He sprinkles the fuel with, 'For <s>Agni</s>, I sprinkle you as acceptable.'
For the sacrificial grass, he says, 'For the earth.'

children.text: darbhamuṣṭim abhyukṣya paścād agneḥ prāgagraṃ nidadhāti ūrṇamradaṃ prathasva svāsasthaṃ devebhyaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Having sprinkled a handful of darbha, he lays it down west of the fire with its tips toward the east, saying, 'Spread out, soft as wool, well-seated for the gods.'

children.text: darbhāṇām apādāya ṛṣīṇāṃ prastaro 'si iti dakṣiṇato 'gner brahmāsanaṃ nidadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Taking some of the darbha grass, he places the seat of the <s>brahman</s> priest south of the fire, saying, 'You are the spread for the seers.'

children.text: purastād agner āstīrya teṣāṃ mūlānyapareṣāṃ prāntair avacchādayan parisarpati dakṣiṇenāgnim ā paścārdhāt ||
children.translated_text: Having spread grass in front of the fire, he moves around it, covering the roots of some blades with the tips of others, to the south of the fire as far as its western half.
He gives the instruction, 'Spread it around.'

children.text: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ prasūtaḥ praśiṣā paristṛṇāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: He says, 'Set in motion by the command, at the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I spread it around.'
In the same way on the north side, arranging the odd-numbered layers.
Where they meet, he makes that part lie from south to north.

children.text: stīrṇaṃ prokṣati haviṣāṃ tvā juṣṭaṃ prokṣāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: When it has been spread, he sprinkles it, saying, 'For the oblations I sprinkle you as acceptable.'
What has been spread but not sprinkled should not be used.
Nor should there be the taking up of fuel that has not been sprinkled.
Nor an oblation that has not been purified.
Nor a sacrificial implement that has not been sprinkled.
On that spread grass he sets down the washed utensils, after they have been passed through the air.
The ladle and the vessel for ghee as well.

children.text: vilīnapūtam ājyaṃ gṛhītvādhiśritya paryagni kṛtvodag udvāsya paścād agner upasādyodagagrābhyāṃ pavitrābhyām utpunāti ||
children.translated_text: Taking ghee that has been melted and purified, placing it on the fire, carrying fire around it, taking it off northward, and setting it west of the fire, he purifies it with the two strainers whose tips point north.
'You are purified by the mind of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.'
'May the god <s>Savitṛ</s> purify you.'

children.text: acchidreṇa tvā pavitreṇa śatadhāreṇa sahasradhāreṇa supvot punāmi iti tṛtīyam ||
children.translated_text: The third time he says, 'With an unbroken strainer, with a hundred streams, with a thousand streams, I purify you well.'
The fourth time is done silently.

children.text: śṛtaṃ havir abhighārayati madhvā samañjan ghṛtavat karātha iti ||
children.translated_text: He pours ghee over the cooked oblation, saying, 'Anointing it with honey, make it rich in ghee.'

children.text: abhighāryodañcam udvāsayati ud vāsayāgneḥ śṛtam akarma havyam ā sīda pṛṣṭham amṛtasya dhāma iti ||
children.translated_text: Having brought it near, he sets it down toward the north, with the words, "Set forth the cooked, unperformed oblation of <s>Agni</s>; sit down upon the back, the seat of immortality."
After placing it behind the clarified butter and adorning it, he purifies it upward in the same manner.
He looks at it with the formula, "not running toward the wife."
With "Arise," he performs the <s>Indra</s>-related act.

children.text: agnir bhūyām iti tisṛbhir upasamādadhāti asmai kṣatrāṇi etam idhmam iti vā ||
children.translated_text: With three verses beginning "May I become <s>Agni</s>," he lays it on again; or with "for this one the royal powers" and "this fuel-stick."

children.text: yunajmi tvā brahmaṇā daivyena havyāyāsmai voḍheva jātavedaḥ indhānās tvā suprajasaḥ suvīrā jyog jīvema balihṛto vayaṃ te iti ||
children.translated_text: "I yoke you with divine brahman for the oblation, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, as a bearer for this one. Kindling you, may we, rich in offspring and rich in heroes, live long, bringing tribute to you."

children.text: dakṣiṇato jāṅmāyanam udapātram upasādyābhimantrayate tathodapātraṃ dhāraya yathāgre brahmaṇaspatiḥ satyadharmā adīdharad devasya savituḥ save iti ||
children.translated_text: On the south side, after setting down the water vessel for the Jāṅmāyana rite, he addresses it: "Hold the water vessel in such a way as <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>, true to dharma, held it at first, at the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>."

children.text: athodakam āsiñcati iheta devīr amṛtaṃ vasānā hiraṇyavarṇā anavadyarūpāḥ āpaḥ samudro varuṇaś ca rājā saṃpātabhāgān haviṣo juṣantām indrapraśiṣṭā varuṇaprasūtā apaḥ samudrād divam ud vahantu indrapraśiṣṭā varuṇaprasūtā divas pṛthivyā śriyam ud vahantu iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he pours in the water: "May the divine waters here, clothed in immortality, golden-colored and faultless in form, the ocean and king <s>Varuṇa</s>, accept the portions that fall together from the oblation. Sent by <s>Indra</s>, brought forth by <s>Varuṇa</s>, may the waters carry it up from the ocean to heaven. Sent by <s>Indra</s>, brought forth by <s>Varuṇa</s>, may they carry up the splendor of heaven and earth."

children.text: ṛtaṃ tvā satyena pariṣiñcāmi jātavedaḥ iti saha havirbhiḥ paryukṣya jīvābhir ācamyotthāya vedaprapadbhiḥ prapadyata oṃ prapadye bhūḥ prapadye bhuvaḥ prapadye svaḥ prapadye janat prapadye iti ||
children.translated_text: With "I sprinkle you, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, with truth by means of truth," he sprinkles around together with the oblations, sips from the living waters, rises, and approaches with the Veda-steps: "Om, I approach earth; I approach atmosphere; I approach heaven; I approach the people."

children.text: prapadya paścāt stīrṇasya darbhān āstīrya ahe daidhiṣavyod atas tiṣṭhāny asya sadane sīda yo 'smat pākatara iti brahmāsanam anvīkṣate ||
children.translated_text: After approaching, he spreads darbha grass behind what has been strewn and looks toward the brahman's seat with the words, "O Ahidaidhiṣavya, I stand away from here; sit in his seat, you who are more skillful than us in cooking."

children.text: nirastaḥ parāgvasuḥ saha pāpmanā nirastaḥ so 'stu yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣma iti dakṣiṇā tṛṇaṃ nirasyati ||
children.translated_text: With "Driven away is Parāgvasu together with evil; driven away let him be who hates us and whom we hate," he throws away a blade of grass to the south.

children.text: tad anvālabhya japati idam aham arvāgvasoḥ sadane sīdāmyṛtasya sadane sīdāmi satyasya sadane sīdāmīṣṭasya sadane sīdāmi pūrtasya sadane sīdāmi māmṛṣad deva barhiḥ svāsasthaṃ tvādhyāsadeyam ūrṇamradam anabhiśokam ||
children.translated_text: Touching that, he murmurs: "Here I sit in Arvāgvasu's seat; I sit in the seat of ṛta; I sit in the seat of truth; I sit in the seat of what is sacrificed; I sit in the seat of what is fulfilled. May the divine barhis not harm me. May I sit upon you as a good seat, wool-soft and free from burning pain."

children.text: vimṛgvarīṃ ityupaviśyāsanīyaṃ brahmajapaṃ japati bṛhaspatir brahmā brahmasadana āsiṣyate bṛhaspate yajñaṃ gopāya yad ud udvata un nivataḥ śakeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: Having sat down with the formula beginning "the sweeping one," he murmurs the brahma-japa to be recited while seated: "<s>Bṛhaspati</s> as brahman will sit in the brahman-seat. O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, protect the sacrifice; may I be able to do what rises from the height and what rises from the hollow."

children.text: darbhaiḥ sruvaṃ nirmṛjya niṣṭaptaṃ rakṣo niṣṭaptā arātayaḥ pratyuṣṭaṃ rakṣaḥ pratyuṣṭā arātayaḥ iti pratapya mūle sruvaṃ gṛhītvā japati viṣṇor hasto 'si dakṣiṇaḥ pūṣṇā datto bṛhaspateḥ taṃ tvāhaṃ sruvam ā dade devānāṃ havyavāhanam ayaṃ sruvo vi dadhāti homān śatākṣarachandasā jāgatena sarvā yajñasya samanakti viṣṭhā bārhaspatyeṣṭiḥ śarmaṇā daivyena iti ||
children.translated_text: Wiping the sruva ladle with darbha grass, heating it with "burned away is the demon, burned away are the enemies; scorched is the demon, scorched are the enemies," and taking the sruva by the base, he murmurs: "You are <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s right hand, given by <s>Pūṣan</s> and by <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. I take you, the sruva, carrier of the gods' oblations. This sruva distributes the homas with the hundred-syllabled jāgata meter; it anoints all the resting-places of the sacrifice. The <s>Bārhaspatya</s> iṣṭi is with divine shelter."

children.text: oṃ bhūḥ śaṃ bhūtyai tvā gṛhṇe bhūtaye iti prathamaṃ grahaṃ gṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: With "Om, bhūḥ; for welfare, for prosperity, I take you for prosperity," he takes the first ladling portion.

children.text: oṃ bhuvaḥ śaṃ puṣṭyai tvā gṛhṇe puṣṭaye iti dvitīyam ||
children.translated_text: With "Om, bhuvaḥ; for welfare, for nourishment, I take you for nourishment," he takes the second.

children.text: oṃ svaḥ śaṃ tvā gṛhṇe sahasrapoṣāya iti tṛtīyam ||
children.translated_text: With "Om, svaḥ; for welfare, I take you for thousandfold increase," he takes the third.

children.text: oṃ jagacchaṃ tvā gṛhṇe 'parimitapoṣāya iti caturtham ||
children.translated_text: With "Om, world-welfare; I take you for immeasurable increase," he takes the fourth.

children.text: rājakarmābhicārikeṣu amuṣya tvā prāṇāya gṛhṇe 'pānāya vyānāya samānāyodānāya iti pañcamam ||
children.translated_text: In royal rites and hostile rites, with "I take you for the breath of that man, for his downward breath, diffused breath, equalizing breath, and upward breath," he takes the fifth.

children.text: agnāv agniḥ hṛdā pūtam purastād yuktaḥ yajñasya cakṣuḥ iti juhoti ||
children.translated_text: He offers into the fire with "In the fire, <s>Agni</s>; purified by the heart; yoked in front; the eye of the sacrifice."
Behind the fire, in the middle region, at the same place, are the preliminary oblations.
To the south of the fire he brings the mingled drops of the clarified-butter oblations into the water vessel.
In the preliminary oblation, the ājyabhāga is the completed oblation and the prosperity of the pacifying rites.
Thus these two are the ājyabhāgas.

children.text: vṛṣṇe bṛhate svarvide agnaye śulkaṃ harāmi tviṣīmate sa na sthirān balavataḥ kṛṇotu jyok ca no jīvātave dadhāti agnaye svāhā ityuttarapūrvārdha āgneyam ājyabhāgaṃ juhoti ||
children.translated_text: In the north-eastern half he offers the <s>Agni</s>-portion of clarified butter, with "To the strong, great, heaven-finding, brilliant <s>Agni</s> I bring the fee. May he make us firm and strong, and may he grant us long life. To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā."

children.text: dakṣiṇapūrvārdhe somāya tvaṃ soma divyo nṛcakṣāḥ sugāṁ asmabhyaṃ patho anu khyaḥ abhi no gotraṃ viduṣa iva neṣo 'cchā no vācam uśatīṃ jigāsi somāya svāhā iti ||
children.translated_text: In the south-eastern half, to <s>Soma</s>, he offers: "You, O divine <s>Soma</s>, watcher of men, have looked out easy paths for us. Lead us to our lineage as one who knows; may you come to our eager speech. To <s>Soma</s>, svāhā."
The oblation is in the middle.

children.text: upastīryājyaṃ saṃhatābhyām aṅgulibhyāṃ dvir haviṣo 'vadyati madhyāt pūrvārdhācca ||
children.translated_text: Having spread clarified butter beneath, with the two joined fingers he cuts off twice from the oblation, from the middle and from the eastern half.
Having poured clarified butter over the cut-off portion, he again pours clarified butter twice over the oblation.
From whatever place he cuts off, he proceeds in that order.
Thus for all the cut-off portions.
Except for the sviṣṭakṛt offering.

children.text: ud enam uttaraṃ naya iti purastāddhomasaṃhatāṃ pūrvām ||
children.translated_text: With "Lead this one upward, to the higher place," the first joined portion belongs to the preliminary oblation.
In this way he offers each preceding joined portion in order.
The homas are made verse by verse with formulas ending in svāhā.

children.text: yām uttarām agner ājyabhāgasya juhoti rakṣodevatyā sā yāṃ dakṣiṇataḥ somasya pitṛdevatyā sā ||
children.translated_text: The northern one of <s>Agni</s>'s ājyabhāga that he offers is addressed to the rakṣas-deities; the one to the south of <s>Soma</s> is addressed to the ancestors.

children.text: tasmād antarā hotavyā devaloka eva hūyante ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the offering must be made between them; they are offered precisely in the world of the gods.

children.text: yāṃ hutvā pūrvām aparāṃ juhoti sāpakramantī sa pāpīyān yajamāno bhavati ||
children.translated_text: If, after offering the earlier one, he offers the later one, it is departing, and that sacrificer becomes worse off.

children.text: yāṃ parāṃ parāṃ saṃhatāṃ juhoti sābhikramantī sa vasīyān yajamāno bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Whichever offering he makes farther and farther onward, compacted together, that one advances; by it the sacrificer becomes more prosperous.

children.text: yām anagnau juhoti sāndhā tayā cakṣur yajamānasya mīyate so 'ndhaṃbhāvuko yajamāno bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Whichever offering he makes on fireless ground, that is blind; by it the eye of the sacrificer is diminished, and the sacrificer becomes liable to blindness.

children.text: yāṃ dhūme juhoti sā tamasi hūyate so 'rocako yajamāno bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Whichever offering he makes in smoke, that is offered in darkness; the sacrificer becomes without radiance.

children.text: yāṃ jyotiṣmati juhoti tayā brahmavarcasī bhavati tasmājjyotiṣmati hotavyam ||
children.translated_text: Whichever offering he makes where there is flame, by that he becomes endowed with brahmanic splendor; therefore it should be offered where there is flame.
Thus, for him, kṣatra belongs to Agni and Soma: this belongs to the Agni-Soma rite.

children.text: agnīṣomā savedasā sahūtī vanataṃ giraḥ sa devatrā babhūvathuḥ yuvam etāni divi rocanāny agniś ca soma sakratū adhattam yuvaṃ sindhūṃr abhiśaster avadyād agnīṣomāv amuñcataṃ gṛbhītān agnīṣomā ya āhutiṃ yo vāṃ dāśāddhaviṣkṛtim sa prajayā suvīryaṃ viśvam āyur vyaśnavat ||
children.translated_text: “O <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, possessing shared knowledge, called upon together, win the songs; together you two have become established among the gods. You two, <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, of one resolve, placed these lights in heaven. You two, <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, released the seized streams from curse and guilt. O <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, whoever gives an oblation to you, whoever prepares an offering for you, he shall attain offspring, good heroic strength, and the full span of life.”

children.text: indrāgnī rocanā divaḥ pari vājeṣu bhūṣathaḥ tad vāṃ ceti pra vīryam śnathad vṛtram uta sanoti vājam indrā yo agnī sahurī saparyāt irajyantā vasavyasya bhūreḥ sahastamā sahasā vājayantā indrāgnī asmān rakṣatāṃ yau prajānāṃ prajāvatī sa prajayā suvīryaṃ viśvam āyur vyaśnavat gomaddhiraṇyavad vasu yad vām aśvāvad īmahe indrāgnī vanemahi svāhā iti ||
children.translated_text: “O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, you adorn the lights of heaven amid the contests. That heroic power of yours is manifest: <s>Indra</s>, who shattered <s>Vṛtra</s>, also wins the prize, when together with <s>Agni</s> he worships. Stirring toward abundant wealth, most powerful, striving for prize with strength, may <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, who belong to offspring, protect us. Possessed of offspring, with offspring and good heroic strength, may he attain the full span of life. The wealth, rich in cows, rich in gold, rich in horses, which we ask of you, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, may we win. Svāhā,” thus.
This is for the oblation belonging to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> on the new-moon day.

children.text: prāk sviṣṭakṛtaḥ pārvaṇahomau samṛddhihomāḥ kāmyahomāś ca ||
children.translated_text: Before the <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, there are the two fortnightly offerings, the prosperity-offerings, and the desire-offerings.
“Full one, behind,” thus, at the full-moon rite.

children.text: yat te devā akṛṇvan bhāgadheyam ityamāvāsyāyām ||
children.translated_text: “The share which the gods made for you,” thus, at the new-moon rite.

children.text: ākūtyai tvā svāhā kāmāya tvā svāhā samṛdhe tvā svāhā ākūtyai tvā kāmāya tvā samṛdhe tvā svāhā ṛcā stomaṃ samardhaya gāyatreṇa rathantaraṃ bṛhad gāyatravartani svāhā ||
children.translated_text: “For intention I offer you, svāhā; for desire I offer you, svāhā; for prosperity I offer you, svāhā. For intention, for desire, for prosperity, I offer you, svāhā. Make the chant prosper with the verse, the Rathantara with the Gāyatra; O Bṛhat, whose course is the Gāyatra, svāhā.”

children.text: pṛthivyām agnaye samanaman iti saṃnatibhiś ca prajāpate na tvad etāny anyaḥ iti ca ||
children.translated_text: And with the conciliation formulas, “On earth, for <s>Agni</s>, for concord,” and also, “O <s>Prajāpati</s>, no one other than you.”

children.text: upastīryājyaṃ sarveṣām uttarataḥ sakṛtsakṛd avadāya dvir avattam abhighārayati ||
children.translated_text: Having spread ghee underneath, for all of them he cuts off once each from the northern side, and he sprinkles the two cut portions twice.
Not the oblations.

children.text: ā devānām api panthām aganma yacchaknavāma tad anupravoḍhum agnir vidvān sa yajāt sa iddhotā so 'dhvarān sa ṛtūn kalpayāti agnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā ity uttarapūrvārdhe 'vayutaṃ hutvā sarvaprāyaścittīyān homāñjuhoti ||
children.translated_text: Having offered the unmixed portion in the north-eastern part with, “We have reached the path of the gods, that which we are able to carry forward. <s>Agni</s>, knowing, shall sacrifice; he is the kindled Hotṛ; he arranges the rites and the seasons. To <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, svāhā,” he offers the all-expiatory oblations.

children.text: svāheṣṭebhyaḥ svāhā vaṣaḍ aniṣṭebhyaḥ svāhā bheṣajaṃ sviṣṭyai svāhā niṣkṛtir duriṣṭyai svāhā daivībhyas tanūbhyaḥ svāhā ayāś cāgne 'sy anabhiśastiś ca satyam it tvam ayā asi ayāsā manasā kṛto 'yās san havyam ūhiṣe ā no dhehi bheṣajam svāhā iti oṃ svāhā bhūḥ svāhā bhuvaḥ svāhā svaḥ svāhoṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā iti ||
children.translated_text: “Svāhā to the well-offered ones; svāhā and vaṣaṭ to the ill-offered ones; svāhā, remedy for the well-sacrificed; svāhā, release from the badly sacrificed; svāhā to the divine bodies. And this, O <s>Agni</s>, is yours, and freedom from curse: you indeed are true, you are this one. Made with an unwounded mind, being unwounded, you carry the oblation. Place remedy in us. Svāhā,” thus; and “Oṃ svāhā, bhūḥ svāhā, bhuvaḥ svāhā, svaḥ svāhā; oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā,” thus.

children.text: yan me skannaṃ manaso jātavedo yad vāskandaddhaviṣo yatra yatra utpruṣo vipruṣaḥ saṃ juhomi satyāḥ santu yajamānasya kāmāḥ svāhā iti ||
children.translated_text: “Whatever of mine has spilled, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, from the mind, or whatever of the oblation has spilled wherever, the scattered drops and splashes I offer together. May the sacrificer’s desires become true. Svāhā,” thus.

children.text: yan me skannaṃ yad asmṛti iti ca skannāsmṛtihomau ||
children.translated_text: “Whatever of mine has spilled,” and “whatever was forgotten,” thus are the two spilled-and-forgotten offerings.

children.text: yad adya tvā prayati iti saṣthitahomāḥ ||
children.translated_text: “Whatever today I have brought to you,” thus are the concluding offerings.
“O lord of mind,” thus, the last one with four ladlings.
He anoints the barhis with the remainder of the ghee.

children.text: pṛthivyai tvā iti mūlam antarikṣāya tvā iti madhyaṃ dive tvā iti agram evaṃ triḥ ||
children.translated_text: “For earth I anoint you,” thus the root; “for atmosphere I anoint you,” thus the middle; “for heaven I anoint you,” thus the tip. In this way three times.

children.text: saṃ barhir aktam ity anupraharati yathādevatam ||
children.translated_text: “The barhis is anointed together,” thus he throws it forward, according to the deity.
He holds the sruva in the fire.

children.text: yad ājyadhānyāṃ tat saṃsrāvayati saṃsrāvabhāgās taviṣā bṛhantaḥ prastareṣṭhā barhiṣadaś ca devāḥ imaṃ yajñam abhi viśve gṛṇantaḥ svāhā devā amṛtā mādayantām iti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is in the ghee-vessel, he causes it to flow together: “The gods who have the flowing-share, mighty with strength, standing on the prastara and seated on the barhis, all praising this sacrifice, svāhā; may the immortal gods rejoice,” thus.

children.text: sruvo 'si ghṛtād aniśitaḥ sapatnakṣayaṇo divi ṣīda antarikṣe sīda pṛthivyāṃ sīdottaro 'haṃ bhūyāsam adhare matsapatnāḥ iti sruvaṃ prāgdaṇḍaṃ nidadhāti ||
children.translated_text: “You are the sruva, sharpened from ghee, destroyer of rivals. Sit in heaven, sit in the atmosphere, sit upon the earth. May I be higher; may my rivals be lower,” thus he sets down the sruva with its handle to the east.

children.text: vi muñcāmi brahmaṇā jātavedasam agniṃ hotāram ajaraṃ rathaspṛtam sarvā devānāṃ janimāni vidvān yathābhāgaṃ vahatu havyam agniḥ agnaye svāhā iti samidham ādadhāti ||
children.translated_text: “With the brahman I release <s>Jātavedas</s>, <s>Agni</s> the Hotṛ, undecaying, touching the chariot. Knowing all the births of the gods, let <s>Agni</s> carry the oblation according to each share. To <s>Agni</s>, svāhā,” thus he lays on a fuel-stick.

children.text: edho 'si iti dvitīyāṃ samid asi iti tṛtīyam ||
children.translated_text: “You are fuel,” thus the second; “you are a fuel-stick,” thus the third.
“You are brilliance,” thus he wipes his face.

children.text: dakṣiṇenāgniṃ trīn viṣṇukramān kramate viṣṇoḥ kramo 'si iti dakṣiṇena pādenānusaṃharati savyam ||
children.translated_text: To the south of the fire he takes three <s>Viṣṇu</s>-steps. With “You are the stride of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,” he brings the left foot up after the right foot.
With “the circuit of the sun,” he turns clockwise.
With “We have gone to heaven,” he looks at the sun.

children.text: indrasya vacasā vayaṃ mitrasya varuṇasya ca brahmaṇā sthāpitaṃ pātraṃ punar utthāpayāmasi ity apareṇāgnim udapātraṃ parihṛtyottareṇāgnim āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvaḥ iti mārjayitvā barhiṣi patnyāñjalau ninayati samudraṃ vaḥ pra hiṇomi iti idaṃ janāsaḥ iti vā ||
children.translated_text: With “By the speech of <s>Indra</s>, and of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, we raise again the vessel established by the brahman,” he carries the water-vessel around behind the fire, and on the north side of the fire, having cleansed himself with “For you are waters, bringers of refreshment,” he pours it into his wife’s joined hands on the barhis with “I send you forth to the ocean,” or with “This, O people.”

children.text: vīrapatny ahaṃ bhūyāsam iti mukhaṃ vimārṣṭi ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "May I become the wife of a hero," she wipes her face.
Saying, "The vows to the lord of vows," he places on a fuel-stick.

children.text: satyaṃ tvartena iti pariṣicyodañci havirucchiṣṭāny udvāsayati ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "Truth with truth," after sprinkling around, facing north, he removes the remnants of the oblation.
A full vessel is the dakṣiṇā (priestly fee).

children.text: nādakṣiṇaṃ haviḥ kurvīta yaḥ kurute kṛtyām ātmanaḥ kurute iti brāhmaṇam ||
children.translated_text: One should not make an oblation without a dakṣiṇā; whoever does so makes a kṛtyā (harmful rite) against himself: so says the Brāhmaṇa.
He feeds the Brahmins with the anvāhārya meal.

children.text: yad vai yajñasyānanvitaṃ bhavati tad anvāhāryeṇānvāhriyate ||
children.translated_text: Whatever in the sacrifice is not followed up is followed up by the anvāhārya.
This is the anvāhārya character of the anvāhārya.

children.text: īḍyā vā anye devāḥ saparyeṇyā anye devā īḍyā devā brāhmaṇāḥ saparyeṇyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some gods are to be praised, other gods are to be attended upon; the Brahmins are gods to be praised and to be attended upon.
By the sacrifice itself he satisfies those who are to be praised, and by the anvāhārya those who are to be attended upon.
Both groups, satisfied, are present for him in the sacrifice, so it is said.
These two, the new-moon and full-moon rites, have been explained.
Through the new-moon and full-moon rites the pākayajñas are explained.
He should offer the vyuddhāra portion from the cooking-pot preparation itself.
Having prepared it by placing on the fire, carrying around the fire, sprinkling with ghee, removing, adorning, and winnowing.

children.text: athāpi ślokau bhavataḥ ājyabhāgāntaṃ prāktantram ūrdhvaṃ sviṣṭakṛtā saha havīṃṣi yajña āvāpo yathā tantrasya tantavaḥ pākayajñān samāsādyaikājyān ekabarhiṣaḥ ekasviṣṭakṛtaḥ kuryānnānāpi sati daivata iti ||
children.translated_text: And there are also two verses: "Up to the ājyabhāgas the earlier procedure; afterwards the offerings together with the sviṣṭakṛt in the sacrifice are insertions, like threads of the ritual procedure. Having brought together the pākayajñas, one should make them with one ghee, one barhis, and one sviṣṭakṛt, even when the deities are different."
By this same rule the amāvāsyā rite has been explained.
Here the second offering is for Indra and Agni.

children.text: tayor vyatikrame tvam agne vratapā asi kāmas tadagre iti śāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the order of those two is reversed, the pacificatory mantras are "You, Agni, are the guardian of the vow" and "Desire is at its beginning."
Where there is no special instruction, he eats the sthālīpāka.
In rites for prosperity, with a calf of similar appearance.
He offers ghee.
He places on a fuel-stick.
He scatters rice, barley, and sesame.
He consumes the juices of milk-rice, boiled rice, and puroḍāśa cakes.
He presents mixed drink and boiled rice.
First comes the triṣaptīya rite.
When water is prescribed, he should go to a vessel of water.
He brings the equipment from the east and the north.
From a place not reached by cattle and from trees.
At the bending of sunrise.
The performance of rites is in the wilderness, to the east and the north.

children.text: uttarata udakānte prayujya karmāṇy apāṃ sūktair āplutya pradakṣiṇam āvṛtya apa upaspṛśyānavekṣamāṇā grāmam udāvrajanti ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the rites to the north at the edge of water, having bathed with the hymns to the waters, having turned clockwise, and having touched the waters, they go up to the village without looking back.
The sitting, binding, bathing, sprinkling, and eating rites are accompanied by saṃpāta drops.
All are to be consecrated with mantras.
For a woman who is diseased, bathed, or sprinkled, beginning from the head, he wipes down to the soles of the feet.
First, having made her step forward, he gives it.
On the three days beginning with the thirteenth, after letting it stand in curds and honey, he binds it on.
He makes her eat.
For one who has taken hold, there are consecratory recitations and oblations.
Behind the fire, on a hide, is the preparation of the oblations.
A lump of dung from a draught ox.
A hide from an animal killed while living.
A stone without a corner.
For bathing and sprinkling rites he also makes the person sip water.
Of things accompanied by saṃpāta drops he eats, or he anoints himself.
For things to be placed on, he restrains the smoke.
The performance of the rite is done with a pure person or pure material.

children.text: purastāddhomavatsu niśākarmasu pūrvāhṇe yajñopavītī śālāniveśamaṃ samūhayatyupavatsyadbhaktam aśitvā snāto 'hatavasanaḥ prayuṅkte ||
children.translated_text: In night rites that include oblations in front, in the forenoon, wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, he sweeps the site of the hall, eats the food of one about to observe a fast, bathes, puts on unworn clothing, and performs the rite.
And in rites for welfare as well.
He carries bali offerings for the worshipped deities to the quarters.
He attends upon each quarter.
Everywhere the fee belongs to the officiant who is in charge.
The water rite is performed three times.
The immediately following items are the same and connected.
The equipment is pacificatory.
Everything belongs to the one who is authorized.
Within the domain, according to the interval.

children.text: pra yaccha parśum iti darbhalavanaṃ prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "Stretch forth the axe," he hands over the darbha-cutter.
Saying, "Of the hostile ones," he trims it.
Saying, "When the śikva has you," he washes it.
The mantra is as stated in the formula beginning "Whatever black one."

Wood of palāśa, udumbara, jambu, kāmpīla, sragvaṅgha, śirīṣa, srakti, avaraṇa, bilva, jaṅgiḍa, kuṭaka, garhyagala, avala, vetasa, śimbala, sipuna, syandana, araṇi, kāśmarya, uktatunya, and pūtudāru is pacificatory.

Citiprāyaścitti, śamī, śamaka, āsavaṃśa, āśāmya, vākā, talāśa, palāśa, vāśā, śiṃśapā, śimbala, sipuna, darbha, apāmārga, a fashioned clod, earth from an anthill, vapā grass, dūrvā tips, rice, and barley are pacificatory.
Pramanda, uśīra, śalalī, upadhāna, śaka, and dhūmā are old or worn materials.
Lead, river lead, lead, iron filings, a lizard's head, and sinews.
Curds, ghee, honey, and water are the liquids.
Rice, barley, wheat, upavāka, sesame, priyaṅgu, and śyāmāka are the mixed grains.
The taking continues until the full taking.
He should apply the later items according to the purpose.

children.text: ihaiva dhruvām eha yātu yamo mṛtyuḥ satyaṃ bṛhat ityanuvāko vāstoṣpatīyāni ||
children.translated_text: "Right here, firm," "Come here," "Let Yama go," "Death," "Truth," and "Great" are the anuvāka and the Vāstoṣpatīya formulas.

children.text: divyo gandharvaḥ imaṃ me agne yau te mātā iti mātṛnāmāni ||
children.translated_text: "The heavenly Gandharva," "This for me, Agni," and "Those two mothers of yours" are the formulas named after the Mothers.

children.text: stuvānam idaṃ haviḥ nissālām arāyakṣayaṇam śaṃ no devī pṛśniparṇī ā paśyati tānt satyaujāḥ tvayā pūrvam purastād yuktaḥ rakṣohaṇam iti anuvākaś cātanāni ||
children.translated_text: "Praising," "This oblation," "Nissālā," "Destroying the non-giver," "May the goddess bring us blessing," "Pṛśniparṇī sees," "Those with true strength," "Formerly by you," "Set in front," and "Slaying the demons" are an anuvāka and expelling formulas.

children.text: ambayo yanti śaṃbhumayobhū hiraṇyavarṇāḥ nissālām ye agnayaḥ brahma jajñānam ity ekā uta devāḥ mṛgārasūktāny uttamaṃ varjayitvā apa naḥ śośucad agham punantu mā sasruṣīḥ himavataḥ prasravanti vāyoḥ pūtaḥ pavitreṇa śaṃ ca no mayaś ca naḥ anaḍudbhyas tvaṃ prathamaṃ mahyam āpaḥ vaiśvānaro raśmibhiḥ yamo mṛtyuḥ viśvajit saṃjñānam naḥ yady antarikṣe punar maitv indriyam śivā naḥ śaṃ no vāto vātu agniṃ brūmo vanaspatīn iti ||
children.translated_text: With the formulas beginning 'The mothers go,' 'producing welfare and happiness,' 'golden-colored,' 'the fires that are without a hall,' 'Brahman born,' likewise 'And the gods,' the Mṛgāra hymns except for the last, 'May they cleanse away from us the burning evil,' 'Do not flow away,' 'They flow forth from Himavat,' 'Purified by the wind with the purifier,' 'Peace and refreshment for us,' 'For the oxen,' 'You first,' 'For me, waters,' 'Vaiśvānara with his rays,' 'Yama is death,' 'All-conquering,' 'Recognition for us,' 'If in the midspace,' 'May strength return to me,' 'Auspicious for us,' 'May the wind blow peace for us,' and 'We address Agni and the forest-trees.'
With 'For the earth, for hearing,' he pours back three times.

children.text: ambayo yanti śaṃbhumayobhū hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śaṃtatīyaṃ ca yadyantarikṣe punar maitv indriyam śivā naḥ śaṃ no vāto vātu agniṃ brūmo vanaspatīn iti ||
children.translated_text: With 'The mothers go,' 'producing welfare and happiness,' 'golden-colored,' also the Śaṃtatīya, 'If in the midspace,' 'May strength return to me,' 'Auspicious for us,' 'May the wind blow peace for us,' and 'We address Agni and the forest-trees.'
With 'For the earth, for hearing,' he pours back three times.
These are the rites connected with pacification.

children.text: ubhayataḥ sāvitry ubhayataḥ śaṃ no devī ||
children.translated_text: The Sāvitrī is used on both sides, and 'May the divine waters be auspicious for us' on both sides.
Wearing an unworn garment, he prepares the pacifying water in a bronze vessel.

children.text: atisṛṣṭo 'pāṃ vṛṣabhaḥ ityapo 'tisṛjya sarvā imā āpa oṣadhaya iti pṛṣṭvā sarvā ityākhyāta oṃ bṛhaspatiprasūtaḥ karavāṇīty anujñāpyauṃ savitṛprasūtaḥ kurutāṃ bhavān ityanujñātaḥ kurvīta ||
children.translated_text: With 'Released, the bull of the waters,' having released the waters, and after asking with 'All these waters and herbs,' when the answer 'All' has been given, he asks permission, 'Impelled by <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, may I do it'; when he is permitted with 'Om, impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, let your honor do it,' he should perform it.

'He should do it with the former,' say the <s>Gārgya</s>, <s>Pārthaśravasa</s>, <s>Bhāgāli</s>, <s>Kāṅkāyana</s>, <s>Uparibabhrava</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, <s>Jāṭikāyana</s>, and <s>Kaurupatha</s> teachers.

children.text: anyatarayā kurvīteti yuvā kauśiko yuvā kauśikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'He should do it with either one,' says the younger <s>Kauśika</s>, the younger <s>Kauśika</s>.
Next are the intelligence-producing rites of the former section.
He fastens the tongues of a parrot, a myna, and a kṛśā bird.
He causes him to eat.
He places pieces of udumbara, palāśa, and karkandhū wood.
He scatters them on.
He eats them.
He gives alms-food to the teacher.
He recites the formula over the ear of one who is asleep.
Approaching, he mutters the formula.
Parched grains mixed with ghee are offered as a whole oblation.
Having offered grains mixed with sesame, he eats them.

children.text: purastād agneḥ kalmāṣam daṇḍaṃ nihatya paścād agneḥ kṛṣṇājine dhānā anumantrayate ||
children.translated_text: Having driven a mottled staff into the ground east of the fire, he recites over the parched grains on a black antelope skin west of the fire.
After reaching the end of the hymn, he gives them.
He offers once.
He gives the staff, the grains, and the antelope skin.

children.text: ahaṃ rudrebhir iti śuklapuṣpaharitapuṣpe kiṃstyanābhipippalyau jātarūpaśakalena prāk stanagrahāt prāśayati ||
children.translated_text: With 'I with the <s>Rudras</s>,' before the child takes the breast he makes him eat white flowers, green flowers, kiṃstya, nābhi, and pippalī, together with a flake of gold.

children.text: prathamapravadasya mātur upasthe tālūni saṃpātān ānayati ||
children.translated_text: For a child first beginning to speak, while he is in his mother's lap, he brings the sprinkled drops to the palate.
He causes him to eat curds and honey.
He makes an initiated pupil recite; this is the rite lasting a hundred rainy seasons.

children.text: tvaṃ no medhe dyauś ca ma iti bhakṣayati ||
children.translated_text: With 'You are our intelligence' and 'Heaven and earth for me,' he eats.
He worshipfully approaches the sun.

children.text: yad agne tapasā ity āgrahāyaṇyāṃ bhakṣayati ||
children.translated_text: With 'What, O <s>Agni</s>, through heat,' at the Āgrahāyaṇī rite he eats.
He worshipfully approaches <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: prātar agniṃ girāv aragarāṭeṣu divaspṛthivyāḥ iti saṃhāya mukhaṃ vimārṣṭi ||
children.translated_text: In the morning, with 'Agni on the mountain,' 'On the aragarāṭa plants,' and 'Of heaven and earth,' having gathered together, he wipes his face.
Next are the accomplishments for a brahmacārin belonging to the former section.
They begin with the udumbara items.
From the brahmacārin's dwelling he takes and places bedding materials.
At an anthill he offers ghee with fat, honey, śyāmāka grain, reed pith, and cotton.

children.text: ājyaśeṣe pipīlikodvāpān opya grāmam etya sarvahutān ||
children.translated_text: Having poured the remainder of the ghee into the anthills, he goes to the village and offers whole oblations.
He gives food, parched grains, and sesame mixtures to brahmacārins.
These are the accomplishments for a village.
As a variant, there are shavings from the bases of posts and bedding materials from assembly halls.
Food is given to the villagers.
Liquor is given to drinkers of liquor.
The udumbara items and the rest, up to the eating, are the accomplishments for all purposes.
He makes the light three times.
He worshipfully approaches.
From the left hand and heart he eats blood mixed with liquid.
This is the pṛśnimantha rite.

children.text: jihvāyā utsādyam akṣyoḥ paristaraṇaṃ mastṛhaṇaṃ hṛdayaṃ dūrśa upanahya tisro rātrīḥ palpūlane vāsayati ||
children.translated_text: He ties up what has been scraped from the tongue, a covering from the eyes, the brain, and the heart in a ladle, and lets it stay for three nights in a palpūlana vessel.
He makes powders.
Having poured the mantha mixture into mixed grain, he eats it mixed with curds and honey.

children.text: asmin vasu yad ābadhnan nava prāṇān iti yugmakṛṣṇalaṃ vāsitaṃ badhnāti ||
children.translated_text: With 'In this, the wealth which they bound' and 'the nine breaths,' he ties on a pair of black beads that has been steeped.

children.text: sārūpavatsaṃ puruṣagātraṃ dvādaśarātraṃ saṃpātavantaṃ kṛtvānabhimukham aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: Having made a human limb with a calf of matching form, furnished with sprinklings for twelve nights, he eats it while facing away.

children.text: kathaṃ mahe iti mādānakaśṛtaṃ kṣīraudanam aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: With 'How for the great one,' he eats milk-rice boiled with an intoxicating substance.

children.text: camase sarūpavatsāyā dugdhe vrīhiyavāvavadhāya mūrchayitvā madhv āsicyāśyati ||
children.translated_text: In a cup, having put rice and barley into the milk of a cow with a calf of the same color, having caused it to thicken and poured in honey, he eats it.
With 'For the earth, for hearing,' he offers.
With 'The calf of <s>Virāj</s>,' the rites continue up to the mantha mixture.

children.text: sahṛdayaṃ tad ū ṣu saṃ jānīdhvam eha yātu saṃ vaḥ pṛcyantāṃ saṃ vo manāṃsi saṃjñānaṃ naḥ iti sāṃmanasyāni ||
children.translated_text: The concord-producing formulas are 'With one heart,' 'That indeed,' 'Know together,' 'Let him come here,' 'Let them be joined with you,' 'Your minds together,' and 'Recognition for us.'

children.text: udakūlijaṃ saṃpātavantaṃ grāmaṃ parihṛtya madhye ninayati ||
children.translated_text: He carries around the village water-gruel furnished with sprinklings and pours it down in the middle.
In the same way he uses liquor-gruel.
He causes them to eat pieces of oyster-shell flesh from a three-year-old heifer.
He makes cooked rice, liquor, and a drinking place furnished with sprinklings.
After the former section come the prestige-producing formulas beginning 'My splendor, O <s>Agni</s>.'
The three beginning with the udumbara item are used.
He recites the formula over the right thigh of a maiden.
He offers the omentum.
He worshipfully approaches <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: prātar agniṃ girāv aragarāṭeṣu divaspṛthivyāḥ iti dadhimadhv āśayati ||
children.translated_text: In the morning, with 'Agni on the mountain,' 'On the aragarāṭa plants,' and 'Of heaven and earth,' he causes him to eat curds and honey.
For a kṣatriya it is mixed with kīlāla; for the others it is kīlāla.
With 'elephant-splendor,' he uses an elephant.
He ties on an elephant tusk.
Having smeared hairs together with lac, he covers them with gold.

children.text: siṃhe vyāghre yaśo havir iti snātakasiṃhavyāghrabastakṛṣṇavṛṣabharājñāṃ nabhilomāni ||
children.translated_text: With 'In the lion and the tiger is fame, the oblation,' he uses navel hairs of a snātaka, a lion, a tiger, a goat, a black bull, and a king.
He uses chips from ten trees of appeasement.

children.text: etayoḥ prātar agniṃ girāv aragarāṭeṣu divaspṛthivyāḥ iti sapta marmāṇi sthālīpāke pṛktāny aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: At daybreak, with these two, 'Agni on the mountain' and 'on the aragarāṭa plants,' and with 'of heaven and earth,' he eats the seven vital spots mixed in a pot-dish.

children.text: akuśalaṃ yo brāhmaṇo lohitam aśnīyād iti gārgyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> says: 'It is improper for a brahmin to eat blood.'
The hair-amulet has been stated.
He causes him to bathe with all of them.
He sprinkles him.
Having sprinkled a four-finger-long blade of grass with a speck from a dust-remover, he crushes it.

children.text: śuni kilāsam aje palitaṃ tṛṇe jvaro yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmas tasmin rājayakṣma iti dakṣiṇā tṛṇaṃ nirasyati gandhapravādābhir alaṃkurute ||
children.translated_text: With 'leprosy in a dog, grey hair in a goat, fever in the grass, consumption in the one who hates us and whom we hate,' he throws the grass away to the south and adorns himself with fragrant proclaiming substances.
The elephant-frightening rites of the preceding section are used.
He turns it back with a chariot wheel furnished with sprinklings.
He advances against it in a vehicle.
With musical instruments.
Having put gravel into leather bags.
With a goad, naked but covered.

children.text: vidmā śarasya mā no vidan adārasṛd svastidā ava manyur nirhastaḥ pari vartmāny abhibhūr indro jayāti abhi tvendra iti sāṃgrāmikāni ||
children.translated_text: The battle formulas are 'We know the arrow,' 'May they not know us,' 'blood not tearing wives away,' 'giver of welfare,' 'anger cast down,' 'around the paths,' '<s>Indra</s> conquers overpowering,' and 'against you, O <s>Indra</s>.'
He offers parched grain mixed with ghee.
With the bow as fuel, he lays a bow as a kindling-stick.
Likewise with an arrow as fuel.
Having wiped the bow that is furnished with sprinklings, he gives it.
The arrow-circling rites of the first section are used.
He ties on the roots of drughnī, ārtanī, bowstring, noose, grass, and plants.
The expulsion formulas begin with 'Away, that one!'
He scatters chaff, husks, rubbish, and shavings.
He recites in response.

children.text: agnir naḥ śatrūn agnir no dūtaḥ iti mohanāni ||
children.translated_text: The bewildering formulas are '<s>Agni</s> [drive] our enemies' and '<s>Agni</s> is our messenger.'
Having taken the chaff with boiled rice, he offers it with a mortar.
Likewise the small grains.
He pounds it out with twenty-one pebbles.
He sacrifices to <s>Apvā</s>.
With 'sharpened,' he lets loose a white-footed female animal furnished with sprinklings.
He should yoke them when they are swelling upward.
With 'This, O <s>Indra</s>,' the rites for the yoked pair continue up to the giving.
With the pair yoked toward the quarters, he worshipfully approaches with 'Homage to the divine weapons.'

children.text: tvayā manyo yas te manyo iti saṃrambhaṇāni ||
children.translated_text: The incitement formulas are 'Through you, O <s>Manyu</s>' and 'what belongs to you, O <s>Manyu</s>.'
Looking at the army, he murmurs them.

children.text: bhāṅgamauñjān pāśān iṅgiḍālaṃkṛtān saṃpātavato 'nūktān senākrameṣu vapati ||
children.translated_text: In the tracks of the army he scatters nooses of hemp and muñja, adorned with iṅgiḍa, furnished with sprinklings, and recited over.
Likewise unbaked vessels.
Having sprinkled grasses with iṅgiḍa, he sets them alight with the Āṅgirasa fire.
They conquer the place over which the smoke spreads.

children.text: ṛdhaṅ mantras tad id āsa ity āśvatthyāṃ pātryāṃ trivṛti gomayaparicaye hastipṛṣṭhe puruṣaśirasi vāmitrāñ juhvad abhiprakramya nivapati ||
children.translated_text: With the mantras 'ṛdhaṅ' and 'That indeed was,' having advanced while offering the enemies in a bowl of aśvattha wood, in a threefold enclosing of cow dung, on an elephant's back or on a human head, he casts them down.
Kings make an altar from ground torn up by a boar.
In that altar the rites continue up to the giving.

children.text: ekeṣvā hatasyādahana upasamādhāya dīrghadaṇḍeṇa sruveṇa rathacakrasya khena samayā juhoti ||
children.translated_text: According to some, having placed the fire on the cremation-ground of one slain by arrows, he offers with a long-handled ladle at the opening of a chariot wheel.
When he has heard that it is to be yoked, he should yoke it.

children.text: yadi cin nu tvā namo devavadhebhyo ity anvāha ||
children.translated_text: He recites in response, 'If indeed you,' and 'Homage to the divine weapons.'
For a vaiśya the rites continue up to the giving.
With 'Through you may we,' he performs it for the leader of armed men.

children.text: ni tad dadhiṣa iti rājñodapātraṃ dvau dvāvavekṣayet ||
children.translated_text: With 'Set that down,' he should make the king look into a water-vessel two by two.
He should not fight the one whom he does not see.

children.text: ni tad dadhiṣe vanaspate ayā viṣṭhā agna indraś diśaś catasro iti navaṃ rathaṃ rājānaṃ sasārathim āsthāpayati ||
children.translated_text: With 'Set that down, O tree,' 'by this support,' '<s>Agni</s>,' '<s>Indra</s>,' and 'the four directions,' he sets the king, together with his charioteer, upon a new chariot.
'The brahman was born' is for discerning life.
Having placed three sinew-ropes on the coals.
When they leap upward, it is auspicious.

children.text: sāṃgrāmikam etā vyādiśati madhye mṛtyur itare sene ||
children.translated_text: He assigns these for battle: death is in the middle, and the two armies are the others.
Death passes beyond those who are going to be defeated, and those who are going to win pass beyond death.

children.text: agreṣūtkucatsu mukhyā hanyante madhyeṣu madhyā anteṣvavare ||
children.translated_text: When the front ones leap up, the chiefs are slain; when the middle ones leap up, the middle men; when the rear ones leap up, the lower men.
Likewise with reeds.

children.text: uccair ghoṣo upa śvāsaya iti sarvavāditrāṇi prakṣālya tagarośīreṇa saṃdhāvya saṃpātavanti trir āhatya prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: With 'loud is the cry' and 'make [him] breathe near,' he washes all the musical instruments, rinses them with tagara and uśīra, strikes them three times after making them furnished with sprinklings, and gives them.

children.text: vihṛdayam ity uccaistarāṃ hutvā sruvam udvartayan ||
children.translated_text: With 'heartless,' having offered more loudly, he turns the ladle upward.
Having sewn a soma-shoot into an antelope skin, he ties it on a kṣatriya.

children.text: pari vartmāni indro jayāti iti rājā triḥ senāṃ pariyāti ||
children.translated_text: With 'around the paths' and '<s>Indra</s> conquers,' the king goes around the army three times.
The soma-shoot of the preceding section has been stated.

children.text: saṃdānaṃ vo ādānena iti pāśair ādānasaṃdānāni ||
children.translated_text: With 'Your binding with a taking,' the taking and binding rites are performed with nooses.
With 'your vital spots,' he arms the kṣatriya.
There is an accession of fearlessness formulas.
With '<s>Indra</s> shall churn.'
With 'rotten rope,' having placed a rotten rope down.
He churns fire from aśvattha and badhaka wood.
With 'smoke,' he recites over the smoke.
With 'fire,' over the fire.
In that wilderness fire he places enemy-destroying arrows made of aśvattha, badhaka, tājadbhaṅga, āhva, khadira, and reed.
The nooses have been stated.
Aśvattha stakes, hempen items, and nets are used.
And badhaka-staffs.
With 'svāhā to these,' he offers to the friends.
With 'to these hard to assail,' using the left hand, he offers iṅgiḍa to the enemies on the badhaka wood.

children.text: uttarato 'gner lohitāśvatthasya śākhāṃ nihatya nīlalohitābhyāṃ sūtrābhyāṃ paritatya nīlalohitenāmūn iti dakṣiṇā prahāpayati ||
children.translated_text: North of the fire, having cut down a branch of a red aśvattha tree, having encircled it with blue and red threads, he has the southern one strike them with 'with the blue-red one.'

children.text: ye bāhav ut tiṣṭhata iti yathāliṅgaṃ sampreṣyati ||
children.translated_text: With 'O arms, rise up,' he gives the instruction according to the characteristic sign.
For the purpose of the oblation there is pṛṣadājya (speckled ghee).
Alternatively, the water-pond rites extend to the giving.
With the water-pond rites there are objects having three joints, shaped like a thunderbolt and shaped like a swelling.
He ties a white-footed one, furnished with sprinklings, with a darbha rope to the support-stick for a <s>kṣatriya</s>.
He throws away a second one.
With 'In this, wealth,' there is entry into the kingdom.

children.text: ānuśūkānāṃ vrīhīṇām āvraskajaiḥ kāmpīlaiḥ śṛtaṃ sārūpavatsam āśayati ||
children.translated_text: He makes him eat rice of the ānuśūka kind, cooked with āvraskaja kāmpīla plants, together with a calf of like color.

children.text: abhīvartena iti rathanemimaṇim ayaḥsīsaloharajatatāmraveṣṭitaṃ hemanābhiṃ vāsitaṃ baddhvā sūtrotaṃ barhiṣi kṛtvā saṃpātavantaṃ pratyṛcaṃ bhṛṣṭīr abhīvartottamābhyām ācṛtati ||
children.translated_text: With 'By the turning toward,' having tied a chariot-rim jewel wrapped in iron, lead, copper, silver, and copper-colored metal, with a golden nave, perfumed, strung on a thread, placed on the barhis, and furnished with sprinklings, at each verse he scatters roasted grains with the two verses ending in 'turning toward.'

children.text: acikradat ā tvā gan iti yasmād rāṣṭrād avaruddhas tasyāśāyāṃ śayanavidhaṃ puroḍāśaṃ darbheṣūdake ninayati ||
children.translated_text: With 'It cried aloud; it has come to you,' in the quarter of the kingdom from which he has been excluded, he lays down in water upon darbha grass a puroḍāśa arranged like a bed.

children.text: tato loṣṭena jyotir āyatanaṃ saṃstīrya kṣīraudanam aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: Then, having spread the place of light with a clod, he eats milk-rice.
From wherever the clod comes, from there come the materials.
At the morning meal they call out over the puroḍāśa of the three.

children.text: bhūto bhūteṣu iti rājānam abhiṣekṣyan mahānade śāntyudakaṃ karoty ādiṣṭānām ||
children.translated_text: With 'Being among beings,' when he is about to consecrate a king, he makes appeasing water in a great river, using the prescribed items.

children.text: sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā dakṣiṇataḥ parigṛhyāyā darbheṣu tiṣṭhantam abhiṣiñcati ||
children.translated_text: Having cooked a pot-offering, having enclosed it on the south, he sprinkles him as he stands on darbha grass.
He makes him mount a couch covered with bull hide.
The two pour together a vessel of water.
While changing garments.

children.text: sahaiva nau sukṛtaṃ saha duṣkṛtam iti brahmā brūyāt ||
children.translated_text: The <s>brahman</s> should say, 'Our good deed together, our bad deed together.'

children.text: yo duṣkṛtaṃ karavat tasya duṣkṛtaṃ sukṛtaṃ nau saheti ||
children.translated_text: 'Whoever shall do a bad deed, his bad deed; our good deed together.'
He makes him eat.
Having mounted a horse, he makes him set out toward the Unconquered direction.
A thousand, with the best village, is the fee.
The rite up to the changing of garments has been explained by the single-king rite.
He sprinkles him on darbha grass upon the couch.
He makes him mount a tiger skin on a higher seat.

children.text: catvāro rājaputrās tālpāḥ pṛthakpādeṣu śayanaṃ parāmṛśya sabhāṃ prāpayanti ||
children.translated_text: Four royal princes, serving as couch-bearers, grasp the bed at its separate feet and bring it to the assembly hall.
A servant washes his feet.
A chief <s>śūdra</s> pours water over them.
He sorts dice that are complete with the winning throw up to the third.
A <s>vaiśya</s>, possessing all his property, attends upon him with 'Release, long-lived one.'

children.text: utsṛjāmi brāhmaṇāyotsṛjāmi kṣatriyāyotsṛjāmi vaiśyāya dharmo me janapade caryatām iti ||
children.translated_text: 'I release for the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; I release for the <s>kṣatriya</s>; I release for the <s>vaiśya</s>. Let <s>dharma</s> be practiced in my realm.'
He proceeds.
He makes him eat.
Having mounted a horse, he makes him set out toward the Unconquered direction.
He goes up to the assembly hall.
He feeds the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> with food mixed with honey.
He makes him eat the juices.
He approaches the buffalo cows.

children.text: kuryur gām iti gārgyapārthaśravasau neti bhāgaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> and <s>Pārthaśravas</s> say that they should make a cow; <s>Bhāgali</s> says not.

children.text: imam indra vardhaya kṣatriyaṃ me iti kṣatriyaṃ prātaḥ prātar abhimantrayate ||
children.translated_text: With 'Increase this <s>Indra</s>, my <s>kṣatriya</s>,' each morning he addresses the <s>kṣatriya</s>.
The joint pouring and the changing of garments have been stated.

children.text: savitā prasavānām iti paurohitye vatsyan vaiśvalopīḥ samidha ādhāya ||
children.translated_text: With 'Savitṛ among impellers,' one who is to serve as household priest, having placed fuel-sticks of the vaiśvalopī kind,
should initiate the <s>kṣatriya</s> with 'Indra, kingship.'

children.text: tad āhur na kṣatriyaṃ sāvitrīṃ vācayed iti ||
children.translated_text: On this they say, 'One should not make a <s>kṣatriya</s> recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.'

children.text: kathaṃ nu tam upanayīta yan na vācayet ||
children.translated_text: How then could one initiate him if one did not make him recite it?
One should indeed make him recite it; one should indeed make him recite it.

children.text: pūrvasya pūrvasyāṃ paurṇamāsyām astamita udakānte kṛṣṇacailaparihito nirṛtikarmāṇi prayuṅkte ||
children.translated_text: At the setting of the sun on the full moon preceding the previous one, clothed in a black garment at the edge of the water, he performs rites for <s>Nirṛti</s>.
In a boat turning to the right he should bury a śāpeṭa vessel.
He sprinkles it with the hymns to the waters.
He abandons the black thing in the waters.
Having put on an unworn garment and sandals, he goes out of the water for the sake of killing life.
Having stayed away, on the following day he makes that rite successful.

children.text: śāpeṭam ālipyāpsu nibadhya tasminn upasamādhāya saṃpātavantaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared the śāpeṭa, tied it in the waters, placed fuel on it, he makes it furnished with sprinklings.
He eats.
Having placed the black thing down, he makes it float away.

children.text: upamucya jaradupānahau savyena jaracchattraṃ dakṣiṇena śālātṛṇāṇy ādīpya jīrṇaṃ vīriṇam abhinyasyati ||
children.translated_text: Having put on worn-out sandals, holding an old umbrella in the left hand and kindling śālā grasses in the right, he throws down an old vīriṇa mat.
Having covered what is uncovered, he offers once.
He strikes the left side, and the sandals too.

children.text: jīrṇe vīriṇa upasamādhāya ayaṃ te yonir iti jaratkoṣṭhād vrīhīñ śarkarāmiśrān āvapati ||
children.translated_text: Having placed fuel on the old vīriṇa mat, with 'This is your womb,' he pours rice mixed with gravel from an old granary.
With 'Bring to us,' he pours parched grains.
With the third verse he does so together with the two joined granaries.

children.text: kṛṣṇaśakuneḥ savyajaṅghāyām aṅkam anubadhyāṅke puroḍāśaṃ pra patetaḥ iti anāvṛtaṃ prapādayati ||
children.translated_text: Having tied a mark on the left leg of a black bird, and a puroḍāśa on the mark, with 'Let the two fly forth,' he makes the uncovered thing fly forth.

children.text: nīlaṃ saṃdhāya lohitam ācchādya śuklaṃ pariṇahya dvitīyayoṣṇīṣam aṅkenopasādya savyena sahāṅkenāvāṅ apsvapavidhyati ||
children.translated_text: Having fastened a blue cloth, covered it with red, wrapped it in white, set a second turban near the mark, he casts it downward into the waters together with the mark on the left side.
With the third verse it is covered; with the fourth it is wrapped.
The variegated rite belongs to the preceding section.
He eats what has been cooked in a nest, with green barhis grass.
He places down smeared sticks a span long.

children.text: nāvyayoḥ sāṃvaidye paścād agner bhūmiparilekhe kīlālaṃ mukhenāśnāti ||
children.translated_text: At the shared place of two boats, west of the fire, on a line scratched in the ground, he eats kīlāla with his mouth.
For three nights he eats the tejovrata food.
That is his food.

children.text: śaṃbhumayobhubhyāṃ brahma jajñānam asya vāmasya yo rohito ud asya ketavo mūrdhāhaṃ viṣāsahim iti salilaiḥ kṣīraudanam aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: With the formulas beginning 'To <s>Śambhu</s> and <s>Mayobhu</s>,' 'Brahman born,' 'Of this gracious one,' 'The red one,' 'Up went his rays,' 'I am the head,' and 'I have overcome poison,' he eats milk-rice with the waters.
The rites ending with the mantha mixture are included.
With the second formula, when about to go away, he should set down an oblation of sacrificial foods.
Then, after returning.
Then, after returning.
Then, while making a request.
Then, while making a request.
There are four supporting sticks made of palāśa rods.
And four made of darbha grasses and upolava grasses.
Having placed that interlaced fuel, eightfold at least, on the session fire, he should offer upon it with ghee.
He should restrain the smoke.
He should eat the residue.

children.text: tam u cen na vinded atha sattrasyāyatane yajñāyatanam iva kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: But if he does not find that, then, at the place of the session, he makes it like a sacrificial ground.
They call the rite '<s>Samudra</s>' (Ocean).

children.text: ambayo yanti śaṃbhumayobhubhyāṃ brahma jajñānam ā gāvo ekā ca me iti gā lavaṇaṃ pāyayaty upatāpinīḥ ||
children.translated_text: With 'The mothers go,' 'To <s>Śambhu</s> and <s>Mayobhu</s>,' 'Brahman born,' 'Hither the cows,' and 'One also for me,' he makes the fevered cows drink salt water.
For those desiring offspring.
He encloses a drinking place.

children.text: saṃ saṃ sravantu iti nāvyābhyām udakam āharataḥ sarvata upāsecam ||
children.translated_text: With 'Let them flow together,' two people bring water in boats, with sprinkling from every side.
In that water he eats cooked mixed grain.
Or a mantha mixture blended with curds and honey.

children.text: yasya śriyaṃ kāmayate tato vrīhyājyapaya āhārya kṣīraudanam aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: From the one whose prosperity he desires, having brought rice, ghee, and milk, he eats milk-rice.

children.text: tadalābhe haritagomayam āhārya śoṣayitvā trivṛti gomayaparicaye śṛtam aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: If that is unavailable, having brought fresh cow dung, dried it, and cooked it in a threefold layer of cow dung, he eats it.

children.text: śerabhaka iti sāmudram apsu karma vyākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: The rite called '<s>Śerabhaka</s>,' connected with the sea, has been explained among the water rites.
He mixes unthreshed grain with a drop from a red she-goat and eats it.
He approaches only this far.
Undoing the knots of grasses, he goes away.
Going up from them, he splashes them with water from a water vessel and wipes his face.

children.text: eha yantu paśavo saṃ vo goṣṭhena prajāvatīḥ prajāpatir iti goṣṭhakarmāṇi ||
children.translated_text: With 'Let the animals come here,' 'Together with your cow-pen,' and '<s>Prajāpati</s> with offspring,' come the cow-pen rites.
He eats the first milk of a cow that has calved, mixed with phlegm.
He gives a cow.
He pours away the water vessel.
Having swept it together and stepped on it with his left foot, he scatters half with his right.

children.text: sārūpavatse śakṛtpiṇḍān guggululavaṇe pratinīya paścād agner nikhanati ||
children.translated_text: For a cow with a calf of the same color, he places balls of dung, guggulu, and salt, and buries them west of the fire.
In the morning he eats from three.
When the alteration is made, the rite is complete.

children.text: āyam agan ayaṃ pratisaro ayaṃ me varaṇo arātīyor iti mantroktān vāsitān badhnāti ||
children.translated_text: With 'This has come,' 'This is the amulet,' and 'This is my varaṇa against enemies,' he ties on the scented objects mentioned in the mantra.

children.text: uttamasya caturo jātarūpaśakalenānusūtraṃ gamayitvāvabhujya traidhaṃ paryasyati ||
children.translated_text: For the last one, having passed four pieces of gold along the thread, bent it down, and thrown it around in three parts.
With 'This fuel,' he places it on the fire.

children.text: tam imaṃ devatā iti vāsitam ullupya brahmaṇā tejasā iti badhnāti ||
children.translated_text: Having plucked up the scented object with 'This deity,' he ties it on with 'By brahman, by splendor.'
The object mentioned in the mantra 'You are the highest.'
With 'Unimpaired are they for you,' the barley amulet.

children.text: prathamā ha vyuvāsa sā ity aṣṭakyāyā vapāṃ sarveṇa sūktena trir juhoti ||
children.translated_text: With the whole hymn of the Aṣṭakā beginning 'The first one indeed has dawned,' he offers the omentum three times.
Of the portions cut off from the pot-cooked offering.

children.text: sahahutān ājyamiśrān hutvā paścād agner vāgyataḥ saṃviśati ||
children.translated_text: Having offered the oblations mixed with ghee together, he lies down west of the fire, keeping silent.
Mentioning the great beings, he gathers himself together.
With 'They yoke the ploughs,' he stretches out a paired plough.
He yokes the right-hand draft animal first.
With 'Come, <s>Pūrṇaka</s>,' the northern one.
The ploughmen yoke the others.

children.text: aśvinā phālaṃ kalpayatām upāvatu bṛhaspatir yathāsad bahudhānyam ayakṣmaṃ bahupūruṣam iti phālam atikarṣati ||
children.translated_text: With 'Let the <s>Aśvins</s> prepare the share; let <s>Bṛhaspati</s> assist, so that it may be rich in grain, free from disease, and rich in people,' he draws the ploughshare across.

children.text: irāvān asi dhārtarāṣṭre tava me sattre rādhyatām iti pratimimīte ||
children.translated_text: With 'You are rich in refreshment, O <s>Dhārtarāṣṭra</s>; may my session prosper in you,' he measures it out.

children.text: apahatāḥ pratiṣṭhāḥ ity apūpaiḥ pratihatya kṛṣati ||
children.translated_text: With 'The supports are driven away,' having struck it with cakes, he ploughs.
Having reached the end of the hymn, he hands it over.

children.text: tisraḥ sītāḥ prācīr gamayanti kalyāṇīr vāco vadantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They make three furrows run eastward, speaking auspicious words.

children.text: sīte vandāmahe tvā ity āvartayitvottarasmin sītānte puroḍāśenendraṃ yajate ||
children.translated_text: Having turned back with 'O furrow, we praise you,' at the northern end of the furrow he sacrifices to <s>Indra</s> with a puroḍāśa cake.
To the two <s>Aśvins</s> with a pot-cooked offering.
They bring the sprinklings into the furrow.
The later ones into a water vessel.
Having set down the oblations of young grass.
He anoints everything.

children.text: yatra saṃpātān ānayati tato loṣṭaṃ dhārayantaṃ patnī pṛcchaty akṛkṣateti ||
children.translated_text: Where he brings the sprinklings, the wife asks the one holding a clod, 'Have you ploughed?'
'We have ploughed,' he says.
'What have you brought?' she asks.

children.text: vittiṃ bhūtiṃ puṣṭiṃ prajāṃ paśūn annam annādyam iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Acquisition, prosperity, nourishment, offspring, livestock, food, and the eating of food,' he says.
He places it to the north in the middle furrow.
Having anointed the northern ploughshare, he sets it aside for yoking in the morning.

children.text: sītāśiraḥsu darbhān āstīrya plakṣodumbarasya trīṃstrīṃścamasān nidadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Having spread darbha grasses on the heads of the furrows, he sets down three cups each of plakṣa and udumbara wood.

children.text: rasavato dakṣiṇe śaṣpavato madhyame puroḍāśavata uttare ||
children.translated_text: Those with sap on the southern furrow, those with young grass on the middle one, and those with puroḍāśa on the northern one.
Having bent back the darbha grasses, he sows.
For a cow with a calf of the same color, having placed balls of dung, guggulu, and salt, he eats them.
A bull is the fee.
With 'Rich in milk,' this is the rite for increase.

children.text: śāntaphalaśilākṛtiloṣṭavalmīkarāśivāpaṃ trīṇi kūdīprāntāni madhyamapalāśe darbheṇa pariveṣṭya rāśipalyeṣu karoti ||
children.translated_text: He makes three heaps at the edges of the kūdī: a heap of peaceful fruits, stones, shaped clods, and anthill earth, wrapped with darbha grass on a middle palāśa leaf.
They eat in the evening.
They sow the remainder again.
Up to the place of apportionment.
He addresses it with a mantra.

children.text: ayaṃ no nabhasas patiḥ iti palye 'śmānaṃ saṃprokṣyānvṛcaṃ kāśī opyāvāpayati ||
children.translated_text: With 'This lord of the cloud is ours,' having sprinkled the stone in the palya, he sows kāśī grass after each verse.

children.text: ā gāvo iti gā āyatīḥ pratyuttiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: With 'Hither the cows,' he rises to meet the cows as they come home.
In the rainy season, at the first downpour, he offers three times to <s>Indra</s>.
With 'Rich in offspring,' he recites the accompanying formula over them as they are being set in place.

children.text: karkīpravādānāṃ dvādaśadāmnyāṃ saṃpātavatyām ayaṃ ghāso iha vatsām iti mantroktam ||
children.translated_text: For the karkīpravāda rites, in the twelve-stranded cord that has received the sprinklings, the formula is as stated in the mantra: 'This fodder here for the calves.'
With 'That which is for your sorrow,' there is the preparation involving clothing.

children.text: tisraḥ kūdīmayīr ūrṇanābhikulāya parihitā anvaktā ādadhāti ||
children.translated_text: He places three woolen kūdī objects, wrapped around a spider-clan, smeared over.
Having smeared with honey a reed-tip wrapped with muñja grass, he throws it among the chaff.

children.text: uta putraḥ iti jyeṣṭhaṃ putram avasāyayati ||
children.translated_text: With 'And the son,' he makes the eldest son sit down.
One who has measured shelter performs the rite for success.

children.text: ardham ardhena ity ārdrapāṇir asaṃjñātvā prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: With wet hands, without making himself known, he gives with 'Half by half.'
Having pushed away the eastern part with the śānta branch,
he moves around toward the fire.
On that new-moon day he places three objects, each a span long.
With 'Into you the resolve,' there is the tasting of the juice.
He performs the rites involving juice.

children.text: stuṣva varṣman iti prājāpatyāmāvāsyāyām astamite valmīkaśirasi darbhāvastīrṇe 'dhyadhi dīpaṃ dhārayaṃs trir juhoti ||
children.translated_text: With 'Praise the height,' on the Prajāpati new moon, after sunset, on the top of an anthill spread with darbha grass, holding a lamp above and over it, he offers three times.
Having brought rice-grains that have received the sprinklings, he moistens them with juices and eats them.
In the same way, on the full-moon day, up to the ājyotā formulas.

children.text: ṛdhaṅmantro tad id āsa iti maiśradhānyaṃ bhṛṣṭapiṣṭaṃ lohitālaṃkṛtaṃ rasamiśram aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: With the ṛdhaṅ mantra, 'That indeed was this,' he eats mixed grain, roasted and ground, adorned with red, and mixed with juice.

children.text: abhṛṣṭaṃ plakṣodumbarasyottarato 'gnes triṣu camaseṣu pūrvāhṇasya tejasāgram annasya prāśiṣam iti pūrvāhṇe ||
children.translated_text: Unroasted, north of the fire by the plakṣa and udumbara trees, in three cups, in the forenoon, with 'By the brilliance of the forenoon I have eaten the foremost part of the food.'

children.text: madhyandinasya tejasā madhyam annasya prāśiṣam iti madhyandine ||
children.translated_text: At midday, with 'By the brilliance of midday I have eaten the middle part of the food.'

children.text: aparāhṇasya tejasā sarvam annasya prāśiṣam ity aparāhṇe ||
children.translated_text: In the afternoon, with 'By the brilliance of the afternoon I have eaten all of the food.'
From a menstruating woman, blood is taken with the fingers.

children.text: yat kṣetraṃ kāmayate tasmin kīlālaṃ dadhimadhumiśram ||
children.translated_text: In whatever field he desires, he places kīlāla mixed with curds and honey.

children.text: saṃvatsaraṃ striyam anupetya śuktyāṃ reta ānīya taṇḍulamiśraṃ saptagrāmam ||
children.translated_text: Having not approached a woman for a year, he brings semen into an oyster shell and mixes it with rice from seven villages.

children.text: dvādaśīm amāvāsyā iti kṣīrabhakṣo bhavaty amāvāsyāyāṃ dadhimadhubhakṣas tasya mūtra udakadadhimadhupalpūlanānyāsicya ||
children.translated_text: With 'The twelfth is the new moon,' he lives on milk; on the new moon he lives on curds and honey. Into his urine he pours water, curds, honey, and palpūlana substances.

children.text: kravyādaṃ nāḍī pra viveśāgniṃ prajābhāṅgirato māyayaitau
children.translated_text: 'The flesh-eating channel entered the fire; with magic these two, the offspring of <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>,

children.text: āvāṃ devī juṣāṇe ghṛtācī imam annādyāya pra viśataṃ svāhā iti ||
children.translated_text: O two goddesses, enjoying the ghee, enter this for the sake of food and eating. Svāhā' - thus.

children.text: niśāyām āgrayaṇataṇḍulān udakyān madhumiśrān nidadhāty ā yavānāṃ paṅkteḥ ||
children.translated_text: At night he lays down āgrayaṇa rice-grains, wet and mixed with honey, as far as the row of barley.
In the same way, having heaped up both kinds of barley,
he eats what has been cooked in a threefold enclosure of cow dung.
According to <s>Kāṅkāyana</s>, this is successful.

children.text: mamāgne varco iti sāttrikān agnīn darbhapūtīkabhāṅgābhiḥ paristīrya gārhapatyaśṛtaṃ sarveṣu saṃpātavantaṃ gārhapatyadeśe 'śnāti ||
children.translated_text: With 'My splendor, O <s>Agni</s>,' having strewn the sāttrika fires with darbha grass, pūtīka, and hemp, he eats what has been cooked on the gārhapatya fire, furnished with sprinklings in all the fires, at the place of the gārhapatya.
In the same way, after bringing the latter two fires together into the former one.
In the same way, with the droṇa jar, the juices are as stated.

children.text: yajūṃṣi yajñe iti navaśālāyāṃ sarpir madhumiśram aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: With 'The yajus formulas in the sacrifice,' he eats ghee mixed with honey in the new house.
With 'Sing at evening,' he eats the second portion.
With the pair of joined formulas, he eats the third.
With the formula to <s>Anumati</s>, he eats the fourth.

children.text: śālām aṅgulibhyāṃ saṃprokṣya gṛhapatnyāsāda upaviśyodapātraṃ ninayati ||
children.translated_text: Having sprinkled the house with his fingers, he sits down on the seat of the housewife and pours out a vessel of water.
With 'Remain right here,' he releases his speech.

children.text: ūrdhvā asya iti vārṣmaṇam audumbaraṃ manthapratirūpam abhijuhoti ||
children.translated_text: With 'Upright is his,' he offers into the fire an udumbara object for increase, resembling a churning-stick.
Having put on the fire an uncounted number of seven-coming cakes,
with 'May <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> for me,' he eats in the morning while the portions are being distributed.
He ties on the bowstring.
Having wiped a staff that has received the sprinklings, he carries it.

children.text: vāyur enāḥ iti yuktayoś citrākarma niśāyāṃ saṃbhārān saṃpātavataḥ karoti ||
children.translated_text: With 'The winds these,' at night, when the two yoked animals are involved, he performs the variegated rite with materials that have received the sprinklings.

children.text: aparedyur vāyur enāḥ iti śākhayodakadhārayā gāḥ parikrāmati ||
children.translated_text: On the next day, with 'The winds these,' he walks around the cows with a branch and a stream of water.

children.text: prathamajasya śakalam avadhāyāudumbareṇāsinā lohitena iti mantroktam ||
children.translated_text: Having set down a chip from the first-born, with an udumbara knife, the formula is as stated in the mantra beginning 'With blood.'

children.text: yathā cakrur itīkṣukāśakāṇḍyā lohitaṃ nirmṛjya rasamiśram aśnāti ||
children.translated_text: With 'As they made,' having wiped off the blood with a piece of sugarcane or reed, he eats it mixed with juice.
Everything is to be of udumbara wood.
With 'Of whom this,' there is the filling of the yokings.
With 'Rise up,' there is the bringing of seed.

children.text: ājyamiśrān yavān urvarāyāṃ kṛṣṭe phālenoduhyānvṛcaṃ kāśīn ninayati nivapati ||
children.translated_text: In a ploughed fertile field, having drawn out barley mixed with ghee with the ploughshare, he pours down and sows kāśī seeds verse by verse.

children.text: abhi tyam iti mahāvakāśe 'raṇya unnate vimite prāgdvārapratyagdvāreṣv apsu saṃpātān ānayati ||
children.translated_text: With 'Toward that one,' in a wide open place, in an elevated and measured spot in the forest, at eastern-door and western-door places, he brings sprinklings into water.
On a black antelope skin he sorts out soma shoots.
He eats what has received the sprinklings together with soma.
When it has blazed up, it is complete.
With 'That, O <s>Savitṛ</s>,' he ties a cord on a young cow.

children.text: saṃ mā siñcantu iti sarvodake maiśradhānyam ||
children.translated_text: With 'Let them sprinkle me together,' mixed grain is put in water from all sources.

children.text: divyaṃ suparṇaṃ ity ṛṣabhadaṇḍino vapayā indraṃ yajate ||
children.translated_text: With 'The heavenly bird,' he sacrifices to <s>Indra</s> with the omentum of a bull-bearing staff.
With the head and feet still attached, having covered the cow-stall with the hide, he feeds the brāhmaṇas with the portions cut off.

children.text: proṣya samidha ādāya ūrjaṃ bibhrad iti gṛhasaṃkāśe japati ||
children.translated_text: After spending the night away, having taken fuel-sticks, he mutters 'Bearing nourishment' in the vicinity of the house.

children.text: savyena samidho dakṣiṇena śālāvalīkaṃ saṃstabhya japati ||
children.translated_text: Holding the fuel-sticks with his left hand and the house-rail with his right, he mutters.
