children.text: ativrajya samidha ādhāya sumaṅgali prajāvati suśīme ahaṃ vāṃ gṛhapatir jīvyāsam iti sthūṇe gṛhṇāty upatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: Having passed beyond, laid on the fuel-sticks, and said, 'O auspicious one, rich in offspring, well-housed, may I live as your householder,' he grasps the pillar and worshipfully approaches it.
With 'What I say,' the action is as stated in the mantra.
Sitting on the housewife's seat, he pours out a vessel of water.
When he is about to set out on a journey, he looks back with, 'Stay right here.'
He makes the cattle stand from good pasture to good pasture.

children.text: dūrvāgrair añjalāvapa ānīya darśaṃ dārśībhir upatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: Having brought water in his joined hands with tips of dūrvā grass, he worshipfully approaches the new-moon rite with the verses belonging to the new moon.

children.text: indrasya kukṣir sāhasras ity ṛṣabhaṃ saṃpātavantam atisṛjati ||
children.translated_text: With 'The belly of <s>Indra</s> is thousandfold,' he lets loose a bull that has been furnished with sprinklings.

children.text: retodhāyai tvātisṛjāmi vayodhāyai tvātisṛjāmi yūthatvāyai tvātisṛjāmi gaṇatvāyai tvātisṛjāmi sahasrapoṣāyai tvātisṛjāmy aparimitapos.āyai tvātisṛjāmi ||
children.translated_text: 'For the placing of seed I let you loose; for the placing of vigor I let you loose; for herdship I let you loose; for flockship I let you loose; for thousandfold increase I let you loose; for immeasurable increase I let you loose.'

children.text: etaṃ vo yuvānaṃ iti purāṇaṃ pravṛtya navam utsṛjate saṃprokṣati ||
children.translated_text: With 'This young one of yours,' having first set the old one in motion, he releases the new one and sprinkles it.
One who desires nourishment sacrifices to <s>Indra</s> on the northern side with a bull.
One who desires prosperity does so with a white one at the full moon.
With 'Truth, the great,' at the Āgrahāyaṇī rite.
Behind the fire, on darbha grass in a khadā vessel, there is a whole oblation.
He eats the second, furnished with sprinklings.

children.text: tṛtīyasyāditiḥ saptabhir bhūme mātar iti trir juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Of the third, with the seven verses beginning '<s>Aditi</s>,' and with 'O Earth, mother,' he offers three times.

children.text: paścād agner darbheṣu kaśipu āstīrya vimṛgvarīṃ ity upaviśati ||
children.translated_text: Behind the fire, having spread a mat on darbha grass, he sits down with 'She who drives away wild beasts.'
With 'Those auspicious ones of yours,' he lies down.
With 'When lying down,' he turns around.

children.text: navabhiḥ śantivā iti daśamyā ud āyuṣā ity upottiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: With the nine verses beginning 'You who are peace,' and with the tenth, 'With life upward,' he rises up.
With 'Up may we,' he steps forth.

children.text: udīrāṇā iti trīṇi padāni prāṅ vodaṅ vā bāhyenopaniṣkramya yāvat te iti vīkṣate ||
children.translated_text: With 'Rising up,' having gone out three steps eastward or northward by the outside way, he looks with 'As far as yours.'
And from an elevated place.

children.text: purastād agneḥ sīraṃ yuktam udapātreṇa saṃpātavatāvasiñcati ||
children.translated_text: In front of the fire he sprinkles a yoked plough with a water vessel, the sprinklings having been applied.
It is the completion of the yoking arrangements.

children.text: yasyāṃ sadohavirdhāne iti juhoti varo ma āgamiṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: With 'In which the seat and oblation-holders are,' he offers, saying, 'A boon will come to me.'
With 'In which there is food,' he worshipfully approaches.
One who desires gold uses an amulet with 'Bearing a treasure.'
Knowing thus.

children.text: yasyāṃ kṛṣṇam iti vārṣakṛtasyācamati śirasy ānayate ||
children.translated_text: With 'In which the black one is,' he sips from the rain-producing water and brings it to his head.

children.text: yaṃ tvā pṛṣatī rathe iti dyauḥ pṛṣaty ādityo rohitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With 'You whom the speckled mare on the chariot,' heaven is speckled and the sun is ruddy.
He gives a speckled cow.
Milk-rice from the speckled cow is the whole oblation.
There is the placing and worshipful approach for rites of nourishment.
For one desiring every wish, with waters; for one desiring every wish, with waters.

children.text: namas te lāṅgalebhya iti sīrayogam adhiśiro 'vasiñcati ||
children.translated_text: With 'Homage to the ploughs,' he pours it over the head at the yoking of the plough.

children.text: namaḥ sanisrasākṣebhya iti śūnyaśālāyām apsu saṃpātān ānayati ||
children.translated_text: With 'Homage to those with flowing axes,' in an empty house he brings the sprinklings into water.
The next is in an old pit, together with house-thatch grass.
In that he makes him sip and bathes him.
According to <s>Śākala</s>, with 'Ten trees.'
Ten friends, muttering, touch him.

children.text: kṣetriyāt tveti catuṣpathe kāmpīlaśakalaiḥ parvasu baddhvā piñjūlībhir āplāvayati ||
children.translated_text: With 'From the kṣetriya disease I free you,' at a crossroads, having tied him at the joints with splinters of kāmpīla wood, he bathes him with piñjūlī plants.
He sprinkles him.
With 'Of the earthly one,' having raised him, he seats the two with their backs joined.

children.text: prāṅmukhaṃ vyādhitam pratyaṅmukham avyādhitaṃ śākhāsūpaveśya vaitase camasa upamanthanībhyāṃ tṛṣṇāgṛhītasya śirasi mantham upamathyātṛṣitāya prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: Having seated the diseased person facing east and the healthy person facing west on branches, in a vaitasa cup, with two churning sticks, he churns a mantha on the head of one seized by thirst and gives it to one who is not thirsty.
Into him he transfers the thirst.
He makes him drink water that has been drawn up.
The mantra is the one whose words include 'the two clothed ones.'

children.text: indrasya yā mahī iti khalvaṅgānalāṇḍūnhananān ghṛtamiśrāñjuhoti ||
children.translated_text: With 'That great one of <s>Indra</s>,' he offers pieces of khalvaṅga, nala, and aṇḍūnhanana mixed with ghee.

children.text: bālān kalmāṣe kāṇḍe savyaṃ pariveṣṭya sambhinatti ||
children.translated_text: Having wrapped hairs around the left side on a speckled stalk, he breaks them apart.
He heats it.
He places it on.
Facing south, with the left hand he churns dust and scatters it around.
He rubs it together.
He places it on.
With 'The sun rising,' he raises it and says, 'Go to the cows; this one.'
At the end of the hymn, with 'They are slain for you.'
He strikes it with darbha grass.
And at midday.
In the afternoon, facing west.
Having cut off a lock of hair, he uses the mortar and the other implements.
With 'From your eyes,' he uses the vībarha plant.
He sprinkles it with a water vessel, the sprinklings having been applied.
With 'Of the antelope,' at the asterism <s>Avanakṣatra</s> he sprinkles with the flame connected with binding, drinking, sipping, and peg-setting.
He throws in barley grains taken once from an unmeasured quantity.
He gives cooked food.

children.text: muñcāmi tvā iti grāmye pūtiśapharībhir odanam ||
children.translated_text: With 'I release you,' in the village he prepares rice with foul-smelling śapharī fish.
In the wilderness, at the asterism <s>Avanakṣatra</s>, he sprinkles with a flame of sesame, hemp, cow-dung, and śāntā.
With 'Release, with the wild-animal repellers,' he bathes him.
For hostile rites, the barhis is made of reeds and cut off on both sides.
From the south he brings the Āṅgirasa material.
Iṅgiḍa oil is the ghee.
The left-hand things are used.
They end toward the south.
On a barren spot sloping southward he performs the rite while facing south.
The rites are accompanied by fire.

children.text: agne yat te tapa iti purastāddhomāḥ ||
children.translated_text: With 'O <s>Agni</s>, that heat of yours,' there are the preliminary oblations.

children.text: tathā tad agne kṛṇu jātaveda ity ājyabhāgau ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, with 'Do that, O <s>Agni Jātavedas</s>,' there are the two portions of ghee.
With 'Drive that man away,' there are the concluding oblations.
They are performed in places of kṛttikā, rokā, rodha, and āvāpya.
With a splinter from a bhāradvāja tree he cuts an Āṅgirasa staff.
With 'From death I,' he sets down the warding implement.

children.text: ya imām ayaṃ vajra iti dviguṇāmekavīrān saṃnahya pāśān nimuṣṭitṛtīyaṃ daṇḍaṃ saṃpātavat ||
children.translated_text: With 'This thunderbolt here,' having bound together a doubled set of ekavīrā nooses and a staff with the third part grasped in the fist, furnished with sprinklings,
he binds with the preceding verses.
'You are a thunderbolt, slayer of rivals; with you today may I conquer <s>Vṛtra</s>.'
'You today, O lord of the forest, we raise up from among the trees.'

children.text: sa na indra purohito viśvataḥ pāhi rakṣasaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Let <s>Indra</s>, placed before us as priest, protect us from demons on every side.'
'The cows have lowed toward us; toward splendor, O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.'
'O breath, preserve breath; O life-breaths, be gracious to life.'
With 'O <s>Nirṛti</s>, by <s>Nirṛti</s> release us from the nooses,'
so saying, he takes up the staff.
With the offering from the cooked food he smears the knot of the girdle.

children.text: ayaṃ vajra iti bāhyato daṇḍam ūrdhvam avāgagraṃ tisṛbhir anvṛcaṃ nihanti ||
children.translated_text: With 'This is a thunderbolt,' from the outside he strikes the staff upward, with its point downward, three times verse by verse.
He should touch within.
The mantra is the one whose words include 'What I eat.'
Whatever vessel he strikes, he says, 'Phaḍ, this one.'

children.text: idam aham āmuṣyāyaṇasyāmuṣyāḥ putrasya prāṇāpānāv apyāyacchāmīty āyacchati ||
children.translated_text: With 'I strengthen the in-breath and out-breath of this son of such-and-such a woman, of such-and-such a family,' he stretches it out.
With 'Those who on the new-moon day,' having bound it on, he puts lead filings into the cooked food and the ornament.
With a staff of defeated bamboo, adorned and about an arm long, he strikes.

children.text: dyāvāpṛthivī urviti paraśupalāśena dakṣiṇā dhāvataḥ padaṃ vṛścati ||
children.translated_text: With 'Heaven and earth, wide,' using a palāśa chip from an axe, he cuts the footprint of the one running to the right.
Afterward, three times crosswise and three times lengthwise.
Having arranged it with the eye.
Having wrapped the dust from the scraping together with palāśa, he throws it into the frying pan.
When they burst, he is laid out.

children.text: paścād agneḥ karṣvāṃ kūdyupastīrṇāyāṃ dvādaśarātram aparyāvartamānaḥ śayīta ||
children.translated_text: Behind the fire, in a pit spread with grass, he should lie for twelve nights without turning around.

children.text: tata utthāya trir ahna udavajrān praharati ||
children.translated_text: Then, rising, he strikes the raised thunderbolts three times a day.
He throws a stone into a river that has no name attached to it.
In hot water he drinks unbroken barley-meal, unchurned, without breathing.
In what way? Three kāśī measures each, for three nights.
Two each for three nights.
One each for six nights.

children.text: dvādaśyāḥ prātaḥ kṣīraudanaṃ bhojayitvocchiṣṭān ucchiṣṭaṃ bahumatsye prakirati ||
children.translated_text: On the morning of the twelfth day, after feeding him milk-rice, he scatters the remains as leftovers among many fish.
When they run together, he is laid out.

children.text: lohitaśirasaṃ kṛkalāsam amūn hanmīti hatvā sadyaḥ kāryo bhāṅgeśayane ||
children.translated_text: Having killed a red-headed chameleon with 'I kill those,' the action is to be performed at once on a hempen bed.
He burns one adorned in red, wearing black, and not previously addressed.
Another stands by with verses of one foot.
Another performs an all-offering limb by limb.

children.text: paścād agneḥ śarabhṛṣṭīr nidhāyodag vrajatyā svedajananāt ||
children.translated_text: Having placed arrow-heaps behind the fire, he goes northward until sweat is produced.
Having returned, adorned with sweat, he offers.
Having placed the chest, breast, and head down, he takes dust from the foot.

children.text: paścād agner lavaṇamṛḍīcīs tisro 'śītīr vikarṇīḥ śarkarāṇām ||
children.translated_text: Behind the fire he places salt, clay, three times eighty vikarṇī pebbles.
Poison is placed on the head.
Drawing it forward with the repelling implement, point downward, he recites along with it.

children.text: pāśe sa iti kośe granthīn udgrathnāti ||
children.translated_text: With 'In the noose he,' he unties the knots in the chest.
With 'That one,' he takes it up.
At a vital spot he digs a pit with a khadira ladle.

children.text: bāhumātram atīva yo iti śarair avajvālayati ||
children.translated_text: With arrows, an arm's length, and with 'Exceedingly who,' he sets it blazing downward.
Having placed it down, gathered it, and swept the clod together with the ladle,
after saying 'I have raised that one up,' he takes a scraper,
or a shadow.
He leads it near.
He recites along with it.

children.text: svastidā ye te panthāna ity adhvānaṃ dakṣiṇena prakrāmati ||
children.translated_text: With 'Givers of welfare, those paths of yours,' he sets out on the road to the right.
He scatters away uncounted pebbles.
Having cut grasses, he attends upon it.

children.text: āre amūḥ pāre pātaṃ na ya enaṃ pariṣīdanti yad āyudhaṃ daṇḍena vyākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: With 'Away, those; fall on the farther side; not they who beset him,' the weapon has been explained under the staff.
Having measured out the face by the diṣṭi measure, he lies down.
Having measured out three steps, he rises.
Three diṣṭi measures.
With 'The departed one, the feet,' having removed it,
he makes him drink.
With 'Your lap,' he steps beyond three measures of water.
With 'Welfare to the mother,' he attends upon it at night.

children.text: indram ahaṃ iti paṇyaṃ saṃpātavad utthāpayati ||
children.translated_text: With 'I <s>Indra</s>,' he raises the marketable object furnished with sprinklings.

children.text: nimṛjya digyuktābhyāṃ doṣo gāya pātaṃ na iti pañcānaḍudbhyo yamo mṛtyur viśvajicchakadhūmaṃ bhavāśarvau ity upadadhīta ||
children.translated_text: Having wiped it, with the two direction-yoked verses, with 'Sing away the fault' and 'Fall not,' for five bulls, he should lay down 'Yama, death, all-conquering smoke of dung, <s>Bhava</s> and <s>Śarva</s>.'
With the last verse, for <s>Rudra</s> of the calf of like form, he offers three times.

children.text: upottamena suhṛdo brāhmaṇasya śakṛtpiṇḍān parvasvādhāya śakadhūmaṃ kim adyāhar iti pṛcchati ||
children.translated_text: With the penultimate verse, having placed lumps of dung from a friendly brahmin at the joints, he asks, 'What does the dung-smoke bring today?'
He answers, 'Good, very auspicious.'

children.text: yuktayor mā no devā yas te sarpa iti śayanaśālorvarāḥ parilikhati ||
children.translated_text: When the pair are yoked, with 'Let not the gods' and 'Your serpent,' he marks around the fertile plots by the sleeping hall.
At the door he cuts grasses from the yoke-opening, furnished with sprinklings.
He breaks apart the fastening.
He buries it.
He lays it down.
Apāmārga blossoms, hoofs turned downward, roots turned away.

children.text: udita iti khādiraṃ śaṅkuṃ saṃpātavantam udgṛhṇan nikhanan gā anuvrajati ||
children.translated_text: With 'Risen,' lifting up and burying a khadira peg furnished with sprinklings, he follows the cows.

children.text: ninayanaṃ samuhya cāre sārūpavatsasyendrāya trir juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Having swept together the outpouring, in the pathway he offers three times to <s>Indra</s> of the calf of like form.
He carries oblations assigned to the directions.
He attends upon each direction.
In the middle he places a fifth, unspecified one.
He pours out the remainder.

children.text: brahma jajñānaṃ bhavāśarvāv ityāsannam araṇye parvataṃ yajate ||
children.translated_text: With 'Brahman was born' and '<s>Bhava</s> and <s>Śarva</s>,' he worships the nearby mountain in the forest.
In another place there are separate oblations for <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Paśupati</s>, <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, and <s>Īśāna</s>.
And in the cow-pen he eats the second portion.
Having placed darbha grass, he fumigates.

children.text: bhūtyai vaḥ puṣṭyai va iti prathamajayor mithunayor mukham anakti ||
children.translated_text: With 'For your prosperity, for your increase,' he anoints the mouths of the first-born male and female pair.
He makes the calves drink three nalada branches.
With a branch and a stream of water he walks around the cows.

children.text: aśmavarma me iti ṣaḍ aśmanaḥ saṃpātavataḥ sraktiṣūparyadhastān nikhanati ||
children.translated_text: With 'Stone is my armor,' he buries six stones furnished with sprinklings at the corners, above and below.
With 'Alasālā,' it is a remedy to be applied.
He buries three tips of silāñjāla plants in the middle of the fertile field.

children.text: hataṃ tardaṃ iti ayasā sīsaṃ karṣann urvarāṃ parikrāmati ||
children.translated_text: With 'The boring creature is slain,' dragging lead with iron, he walks around the field.
He scatters stones over it.

children.text: tardam avaśirasaṃ vadanāt keśena samuhyorvarāmadhye nikhanati ||
children.translated_text: Having swept together a headless boring creature from its mouth with a hair, he buries it in the middle of the field.
And this has been stated in the rite.
He carries the offerings to <s>Āśā</s>, to the lord of <s>Āśā</s>, to the <s>Aśvins</s>, and to <s>Kṣetrapati</s>.
When he performs this for these deities, he should stand restrained in speech until sunset.
With 'The paths,' having gone around, he should place it down.
He gives it.

children.text: yasyās te yat te devī viṣāṇā pāśān ity unmocanapratirūpaṃ saṃpātavantaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: With 'That of yours, that of yours, O goddess,' and with 'the horns, the nooses,' he makes the rite, furnished with sprinklings, in the form of an unfastening.
For one bound by speech, he makes a line around the ground.

children.text: āyana iti śamanam antarā hradaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: With 'going,' he performs the pacification between the pools.
And in the hall.
With avakā plants he stretches them around the hall.
He gives it to one who is being cursed.
He washes what has been burned.
With 'The great earth indeed,' he makes him take hold of the crossings.
From afar he fastens a boat furnished with sprinklings, a boat-amulet.

children.text: prapatha iti naṣṭaiṣiṇāṃ prakṣālitābhyaktapāṇipādānāṃ dakṣiṇān pāṇīn nimṛjyotthāpayati ||
children.translated_text: With 'the broad road,' for those seeking what is lost, after their hands and feet have been washed and anointed, he wipes their right hands and raises them up.
Thus also for those furnished with sprinklings.
Having wiped, he throws and scatters twenty-one pebbles at a crossroads.
The mantra is the one whose words include 'having paid homage.'
For the aṃholiṅga formulas, there is touching of the waters, foods, and oblations, and attendance upon the <s>Āditya</s>.
He himself eats the oblations.
With 'All the gods,' there are rites for long life.
At the pot-cooked offering, he brings forward lumps of ghee and eats them.

children.text: asmin vasu yad ābadhnan nava prāṇān iti yugmakṛṣṇalam ādiṣṭānāṃ sthālīpāka ādhāya badhnāti ||
children.translated_text: With 'In this, O <s>Vasu</s>,' and 'What they bound, the nine breaths,' having placed a paired kṛṣṇala on the pot-cooked offering of those prescribed, he fastens it.
He makes him eat.

children.text: āyurdā iti godānaṃ kārayiṣyan saṃbhārān saṃbharati ||
children.translated_text: With 'Giver of life,' when he is going to have the godāna performed, he gathers the materials.

children.text: amamrim ojomānīṃ dūrvām akarṇam aśmamaṇḍalam ānaḍuhaśakṛtpiṇḍaṃ ṣaḍ darbhaprāntāni kaṃsam ahate vasane śuddham ājyam śāntā oṣadhīr navam udakumbham ||
children.translated_text: They are amamri, ojomānī, dūrvā grass, an uncut stone disk, a lump of bull's dung, six tips of darbha grass, a bronze vessel, a clean unworn garment, purified ghee, pacifying herbs, and a new water jar.
Outside, having laid down eastward fuel from a pacifying tree,

children.text: parisamuhya paryukṣya paristīrya barhir udapātram upasādya paricaraṇenājyaṃ paricarya ||
children.translated_text: having swept around, sprinkled around, spread the barhis, set down the water vessel, and prepared the ghee with the attendant implement,
having offered the regular preliminary oblations and the two portions of ghee,

children.text: paścād agneḥ prāṅmukha upaviśyānvārabdhāya śāntyudakaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: he sits east-facing west of the fire and prepares pacifying water for the one who has taken hold of him.
There he applies this hymn.
He sprinkles the fire three times and sprinkles around it three times.

children.text: triḥ kārayamāṇam ācāmayati ca samprokṣati ca ||
children.translated_text: He makes the person for whom the rite is performed sip water three times and sprinkles him three times.

children.text: śakṛtpiṇḍasya sthālarūpaṃ kṛtvā suhṛde brāhmaṇāya prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: Having made the dung lump into the form of a dish, he gives it to a friendly Brahmin.

children.text: tat suhṛd dakṣiṇato 'gner udaṅmukha āsīno dhārayati ||
children.translated_text: That friend, seated north-facing to the south of the fire, holds it.
Then he performs the rite for this one who has taken hold of him.

children.text: āyurdā ity anena sūktenājyaṃ juhvan mūrdhni saṃpātān ānayati ||
children.translated_text: With the hymn beginning 'Giver of life,' while offering ghee, he brings the sprinklings onto the head.

children.text: dakṣiṇe pāṇāvaśmamaṇḍala udapātra uttarasaṃpātān sthālarūpa ānayati ||
children.translated_text: Into the stone disk in the right hand, into the water vessel, and into the dish-form he brings the later sprinklings.
And having placed amamri and ojomānī in the water vessel,
having poured together in one place dūrvā grass, pacifying water, and warm water in the dish-form,

children.text: āyam agan savitā kṣureṇa ity udapātram anumantrayate ||
children.translated_text: with 'This <s>Savitṛ</s> has come with the razor,' he addresses the water vessel.
With '<s>Aditi</s> is the beard,' he moistens it.

children.text: yat kṣureṇa ity udakpattraṃ kṣuram adbhi ścotya triḥ pramārṣṭi ||
children.translated_text: With 'What with the razor,' having sprinkled the water-blade, the razor, with water, he wipes it three times.

children.text: yenāvapat iti dakṣiṇasya keśapakṣasya darbhapiñjūlyā keśān abhinidhāya pracchidya sthālarūpe karoti ||
children.translated_text: With 'By which he shaved,' having placed the hairs of the right side-lock on a tuft of darbha grass, he cuts them off and puts them in the dish-form.
In just the same way he does the second.
Thus the third.
In just the same way he does the northern side-lock.

children.text: viśve devā iti viśvān āyuṣkāmo yajate ||
children.translated_text: With 'All the gods,' one desiring long life sacrifices to all.
He attends upon them.
With 'This, O people,' one desiring nourishment sacrifices to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>.
One desiring success does so.
With '<s>Indra</s>, enjoy,' one desiring strength sacrifices to <s>Indra</s>.
With '<s>Indra</s> I,' one desiring merchandise does so.

children.text: ud enam uttaraṃ naya yo 'smān indraḥ sutrāmā iti grāmakāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With 'Lead him upward, higher,' and 'May <s>Indra</s>, good protector, protect us,' one desiring a village does so.
This is an increase of village prosperity.
With 'Splendor for me, O <s>Indra</s>,' one desiring fame does so.
With 'Waters for me,' one desiring wide vision does so.
With 'Come here,' one desiring a wife does so.
With 'Of bull-like <s>Indra</s>,' one desiring virility does so.

children.text: ā tvāhārṣam dhruvā dyaur iti dhrauvyakāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With 'I have brought you; firm is heaven,' one desiring stability does so.

children.text: tyam ū ṣu trātāram ā mandrair iti svastyayanakāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With 'That protector, with gladdening songs,' one desiring well-being does so.

children.text: sāmās tvāgne abhyarcata ity agniṃ saṃpatkāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With 'Let the chants praise you, O <s>Agni</s>,' one desiring success sacrifices to <s>Agni</s>.
With 'On the earth,' the mantra is as stated in the text.

children.text: tad id āsa dhītī vā itīndrāgnī ||
children.translated_text: With 'That indeed was a thought,' he sacrifices to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.

children.text: yasyedam ā rajo 'tharvāṇaṃ aditir dyaur diteḥ putrāṇām bṛhaspate savitar ity abhyuditaṃ brahmacāriṇaṃ bodhayati ||
children.translated_text: With 'Whose this expanse,' '<s>Atharvan</s>,' '<s>Aditi</s> is heaven,' 'of <s>Diti</s>'s sons,' '<s>Bṛhaspati</s>,' and '<s>Savitṛ</s>,' he awakens a brahmacārin who has been overtaken by sunrise.

children.text: dhātā dadhātu prajāpatir janayati anv adya no yan na indro yayor ojasā viṣṇor nu kaṃ agnāviṣṇū somārudrā sinīvāli bṛhaspatir naḥ yat te devā akṛṇvan pūrṇā paścāt prajāpate abhyarcata ko asyā na iti prajāpatim ||
children.translated_text: With '<s>Dhātṛ</s> shall place,' '<s>Prajāpati</s> generates,' 'after us today,' 'what <s>Indra</s> for us,' 'by the strength of those two,' 'now of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,' '<s>Agni</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>,' '<s>Soma</s> and <s>Rudra</s>,' '<s>Sinīvālī</s>,' '<s>Bṛhaspati</s> for us,' 'what the gods made for you,' 'full behind,' '<s>Prajāpati</s>, praise,' and 'who of this one,' he sacrifices to <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: agna indraś ca iti mantroktān sarvakāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With '<s>Agni</s> and <s>Indra</s>,' one desiring all things sacrifices to the deities named in the mantras.

children.text: ya īśe ye bhakṣayanta itīndrāgnī lokakāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With 'Who rules' and 'Who eat,' one desiring the world sacrifices to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.
He gives food first.
The bringing near of the animals is last.
The preliminary oblations with the vapā are joined to it.
With 'Sing in the evening,' having brought <s>Atharvan</s> around, he eats.

children.text: abhayaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī śyeno 'si iti pratidiśaṃ saptarṣīn abhayakāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With 'Fearlessness, O heaven and earth' and 'You are a falcon,' one desiring fearlessness sacrifices to the seven seers in each direction.

children.text: uttareṇa dīkṣitasya vā brahmacāriṇo vā daṇḍapradānaṃ ||
children.translated_text: After this comes the giving of a staff to an initiated man or to a brahmacārin.

children.text: dyauś ca ma iti dyāvāpṛthivyai viriṣyati ||
children.translated_text: With the mantra beginning, "Heaven and earth, and me," he acts for <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>.

children.text: yo agnāv iti rudrān svastyayanakāmaḥ svastyayanakāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With the mantra beginning, "Who in the fire," one who desires svastyayana (well-being and protection) acts for the <s>Rudras</s>.
